title: [SWARM-AUTOPILOT-P3] Add warehouse forensic diff and incident replay analysis control plane
description:
Extend the warehouse lifecycle surfaces with operator-facing forensic comparison tools that answer what changed between healthy and failing swarm runs.

Goals:
- compare healthy reference cohorts against degraded, blocked, and contaminated cohorts without manual JSON diffing
- preserve replay-ready evidence paths, normalized fingerprints, worker and topology pivots, and remediation hints for incident triage
- derive compact root-cause and counterexample hypotheses from real warehouse evidence without mutating live swarm policy
- surface forensic comparison readiness and replay recommendations as advisory-only operator evidence
- maintain fail-closed behavior for stale references, contradictory cohort membership, missing raw artifact paths, local fallback contamination, and unsupported mutation claims

Deliver this as a granular control plane with contracts, proof-only scripts, comparison receipts, replay recipes, operator integration, and a no-mock truth surface.
close_reason: Done: all child beads landed and no-mock truth gates are closed.

title: [REVIEW] Replace non-deterministic SystemTime::now() in shadow adoption gates
description:
CRITICAL: shadow_adoption_gates.rs uses SystemTime::now() at multiple locations (lines 61, 77, 93, 109, 125, 129) violating deterministic principles.

File: crates/franken-engine/src/shadow_adoption_gates.rs:61,77,93,109,125,129

The AdoptionGate.last_check and ShadowAdoptionGates.generated_at fields use SystemTime::now() making gate status non-deterministic across runs.

Reproduction: Create two ShadowAdoptionGates instances and compare - timestamps will differ.

Fix: Replace with configurable timestamp injection or remove timestamp tracking entirely for deterministic behavior.
close_reason: done: Already resolved as part of bd-1xybt. shadow_adoption_gates.rs SystemTime::now() usage was replaced with SecurityEpoch::GENESIS in commit 1aa4c7eb, converting all last_check and generated_at fields to deterministic SecurityEpoch types.

title: [AUDIT-CONFORMANCE] shadow_decision_composer: advisory-only output contract lacks harness
description:
File: crates/franken-engine/src/shadow_decision_composer.rs:1-6,21-31,33-47,49-60,396-575
Documented invariant: "recommendations name commands for a human or separate agent to run, but this module never executes them"; schemas are stable; composition is deterministic and bounded by required source keys and max recommendations.
Implementation site: compose_shadow_decision, normalize_journal_event, render_commands_txt/render_events_jsonl outputs.
Why a harness matters: Scenario unit tests do not form a conformance corpus for the public advisory contract. A regression could emit executable mutation commands, change stable schema fields, exceed recommendation caps, or produce nondeterministic source/error ordering while ordinary scenario tests still pass.
Suggested harness shape: Golden conformance fixtures for confirmed/degraded/blocked/contaminated truth states. Assert commands.txt is inert preview text only, recommendation count never exceeds the cap, required-source omissions map to stable error codes, output schemas/keys are stable, and two runs with identical inputs produce identical JSON/notice/event artifacts.
Effort: medium
close_reason: done: added conformance harness covering advisory-only output contract

title: [REVIEW] Shadow replay verifier panics on zero batch size
description: [MEDIUM] ReplayConfig exposes max_events_per_batch as a public usize in crates/franken-engine/src/shadow_replay_verifier.rs:172. replay_events copies it directly at lines 444-447 and calls (0..events.len()).step_by(batch_size). If a caller builds ReplayConfig { max_events_per_batch: 0, ..Default::default() }, replay_export panics instead of returning ReplayVerificationError. Repro: construct ShadowReplayVerifier::new(ReplayConfig { max_events_per_batch: 0, ..ReplayConfig::default() }, 300) and replay a fixture with at least one event; step_by(0) panics. Fix should validate config in new/replay_events and return InvalidCheckpoint/ValidationFailed for zero batch sizes.
close_reason: done: Duplicate of bd-1vxzj. This same zero batch size panic issue was already fixed in commit ec43a1c7 which added validation to ShadowReplayVerifier::new() to prevent max_events_per_batch=0 and return InvalidConfiguration error instead of allowing step_by(0) to panic.

title: [10.1] Add donor-extraction scope document with explicit exclusions for V8/QuickJS semantic harvesting.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.1 donor-extraction governance (plus section 4.1 spec-first hybrid bootstrap decision contract).

## What
Define a normative donor-extraction scope document that permits behavior-level semantic harvesting from donor corpora while explicitly forbidding architectural/runtime transplantation into FrankenEngine core.

## Rationale
The fastest way to lose de novo engine integrity is accidental architecture import from donor runtimes. This bead creates an explicit legal/illegal boundary so teams can harvest semantics for compatibility without reintroducing binding-led design patterns.

## Detailed Requirements
1. Define a positive allowlist of permitted donor outputs (observable semantics, compatibility edge cases, conformance vectors, lockstep fixture seeds).
2. Define a strict denylist of prohibited imports (runtime architecture internals, scheduling model assumptions, hidden compatibility shims, binding-led execution paths).
3. Define provenance documentation rules for every donor-informed change (source corpus reference, extracted behavior statement, native implementation mapping).
4. Define extraction workflow stages (`collect -> normalize -> approve -> integrate`) with clear ownership and artifact checkpoints.
5. Define PR/review gating checklist that must pass before donor-informed code merges.
6. Define CI guardrails and audit logging requirements for donor-scope exceptions and overrides.
7. Define exception policy with mandatory ADR linkage, explicit rollback path, and time-bounded approval window.
8. Define anti-drift policy ensuring donor guidance informs semantics only, never runtime architecture ownership boundaries.

## Dependencies
- Inputs from plan architecture doctrine and split-contract constraints.
- Downstream dependency for semantic donor spec, architecture synthesis, and feature-parity tracker work.

## Verification Requirements
- Governance tests/checklists proving donor scope controls are enforced in review and CI policy paths.
- Integration/e2e policy tests showing prohibited donor patterns are blocked with deterministic failure reasons.
- Regression checks that donor-informed changes preserve de novo architecture constraints.
- Structured audit logging assertions for exceptions and override decisions (`trace_id`, `decision_id`, `policy_id`, `component`, `event`, `outcome`, `error_code`).

## User/Operator Value
- Prevents architecture drift and hidden compatibility debt.
- Preserves trust in native-first claims while retaining compatibility insight velocity.
- Produces auditable rationale for donor-material use decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid/adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds/fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build/test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation/test workloads.
notes: Delivered donor-extraction governance contract at docs/DONOR_EXTRACTION_SCOPE.md with explicit allowlist/denylist, provenance record schema, staged workflow (collect->normalize->approve->integrate), PR gate checklist, CI/audit failure codes, strict exception policy, anti-drift controls, and operator runbook. Added README link and checked plan item in PLAN_TO_CREATE_FRANKEN_ENGINE.md. Added deterministic policy suite script scripts/run_donor_extraction_scope_suite.sh (modes check|test|ci) emitting artifacts under artifacts/donor_extraction_scope/<timestamp>/. Validation: bash -n scripts/run_donor_extraction_scope_suite.sh PASS; ./scripts/run_donor_extraction_scope_suite.sh ci PASS with manifest artifacts/donor_extraction_scope/20260222T011245Z/run_manifest.json and events artifacts/donor_extraction_scope/20260222T011245Z/donor_extraction_scope_events.jsonl.

## Enriched Self-Contained Context (Plan Sections 4, 4.1, 8.7)

### Background
FrankenEngine's execution strategy (Section 4.1) is 'Spec-First Hybrid Bootstrap': use V8/QuickJS only as semantic donor corpora, NOT as architectural blueprints. The plan states: 'Use donor engines to extract behavior specifications and conformance vectors, not architectural blueprints. Implement from extracted specifications in native Rust crates; never line-by-line translate donor code.'

### Document Requirements
1. **In-scope extractions**: Enumerate observable behaviors being harvested: ES2020 normative semantics, Promise/microtask ordering, closure/scope behavior, prototype chain semantics, property descriptor behavior, iterator/generator protocols, module resolution rules.
2. **Explicit exclusions**: What is NOT ported: V8 hidden classes/inline caches, Turbofan/Ignition pipeline design, QuickJS bytecode format, V8/QuickJS GC algorithms, internal object layouts, engine-specific optimization heuristics.
3. **Extraction methodology**: Behavioral observation via test cases, not code reading. Clear boundary between 'learning from donor behavior' (OK) and 'copying donor architecture' (NOT OK).
4. **Legal/IP boundary**: Only observable behavioral specifications used, not copyrighted internal implementations.

### Traceability Requirements
- Each implementation bead in 10.2 (VM Core) should trace to an extraction in this document or to a FrankenEngine-original design decision
- Version-controlled with updates when new extraction domains are added
- Cross-reference: the semantic donor spec document (bd-3u5) consumes this scope document as its input contract

title: [10.11] Add deterministic fallback protocol when anti-entropy reconciliation cannot peel/resolve.
description:
## Plan Reference
- **Section**: 10.11 item 31 (FrankenSQLite-Inspired Runtime Systems Track)
- **9G Cross-ref**: 9G.10 — O(Delta) anti-entropy + proof-carrying recovery
- **Top-10 Links**: #5 (Supply-chain trust fabric), #10 (Provenance + revocation fabric)

## What
Add a deterministic fallback protocol when anti-entropy reconciliation cannot peel or resolve. When the IBLT-based reconciliation (bd-2n6) fails to decode the set difference, the system must fall back to a simpler, guaranteed-convergence protocol rather than leaving state inconsistent.

## Detailed Requirements
1. Define a \`ReconciliationFallback\` protocol that activates when IBLT peeling fails:
   - Step 1: Both nodes exchange sorted lists of object hashes (Tier 2 ContentHash) for the reconciliation scope.
   - Step 2: Compute set difference via merge-join of sorted lists (O(n log n) or O(n) with pre-sorted persistence).
   - Step 3: Request and transfer missing objects (same as normal reconciliation).
   - Step 4: Verify received objects.
2. Fallback triggers:
   - IBLT peel failure (too many differences for the IBLT size).
   - IBLT peel produces inconsistent results (hash verification failure on decoded objects).
   - Reconciliation timeout (exceeds convergence SLO without completing).
   - MMR consistency proof failure (suggests stream divergence, not just missing objects).
3. Fallback scope: the fallback operates on the same object scope as the failed reconciliation attempt. It does not re-reconcile the entire history unless specifically requested.
4. Performance bounds: the fallback is O(n) in communication (full hash list exchange) rather than O(Delta), but it guarantees convergence. The protocol should support incremental transfer (hash ranges) to reduce overhead for large sets.
5. Evidence: every fallback activation emits a structured evidence entry: \`fallback_id\`, \`trigger_reason\`, \`original_reconciliation_id\`, \`scope_size\`, \`differences_found\`, \`objects_transferred\`, \`duration_ms\`, \`epoch_id\`, \`trace_id\`.
6. Fallback frequency monitoring: if fallbacks occur more than a configurable threshold (default: >5% of reconciliation attempts), the system emits a \`FallbackRateExceeded\` alert feeding into the regime detector (bd-gr1). This indicates the IBLT is undersized or the difference rate is abnormally high.
7. Determinism: the fallback protocol must produce identical results regardless of which node initiates it (sorted hash comparison ensures order-independent convergence).

## Rationale
IBLT-based reconciliation is efficient but probabilistic: it fails when the actual difference exceeds the IBLT capacity. The 9G.10 contract requires that reconciliation always converges, even when the efficient path fails. The deterministic fallback guarantees convergence at the cost of higher communication overhead. Without this fallback, reconciliation failures would leave nodes in inconsistent states, violating the trust fabric's convergence SLO and potentially causing security-critical state divergence.

## Testing Requirements
- **Unit tests**: Verify fallback activates on IBLT peel failure. Verify sorted-list difference computation is correct. Verify fallback produces the same result as IBLT would for small differences.
- **Property tests**: Generate set pairs with large differences that overwhelm the IBLT; verify fallback correctly identifies all differences.
- **Integration tests**: Configure an undersized IBLT, inject a large difference, verify IBLT fails and fallback activates, verify convergence, verify evidence emission.
- **Frequency monitoring tests**: Trigger repeated fallbacks and verify the \`FallbackRateExceeded\` alert fires at the configured threshold.
- **Determinism tests**: Run fallback from both node perspectives and verify identical difference computation.
- **Logging/observability**: Fallback events carry all structured fields for monitoring and debugging.

## Implementation Notes
- Sorted hash list exchange can use a streaming protocol to avoid memory pressure for large sets.
- Consider a hybrid approach: binary-search-based range narrowing before full list exchange to reduce transfer size.
- The fallback should reuse the same object transfer and verification logic as the normal reconciliation path.
- Fallback frequency should be tracked as a metric in the bulkhead/scheduler observability.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: bd-2n6 (anti-entropy reconciliation triggers the fallback), bd-4hf (hash strategy for object identity), bd-hli (remote capability gate), bd-289 (remote in-flight bulkhead).
- Blocks: bd-2j3 (proof-carrying recovery for fallback outcomes).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Implement the full objective with deterministic behavior, explicit failure semantics, and safe fallback/rollback rules.
- Add focused unit tests for normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
- Add integration and/or end-to-end test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions, degraded mode, and recovery behavior with deterministic fixtures.
- Emit structured logs with stable keys (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and assert critical events in tests.
- Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, evidence pointers, replay pointers, benchmark/check outputs) plus clear operator verification steps.
- Ensure heavy Rust build/test execution paths are documented and run through rch wrappers when implementation begins.

title: [review][baseline_interpreter] Fix batch-39 global builtin argument indexing
description: Review of commit d425824f found that the new batch-39 upper-case global builtin paths read the wrong registers. The existing lower-case global implementations for isNaN/isFinite/parseInt/parseFloat read their first argument from args.start at crates/franken-engine/src/baseline_interpreter.rs:8443, 8471, 8502, and 8568. The new mapped capabilities for indices 377-380 at lines 19504-19507 route to ParseInt/ParseFloat/IsNaN/IsFinite, but those arms read the first argument from args.start + 1 at lines 18748, 18817, 18884, and 18903, and their radix/second argument from args.start + 2 at line 18759. With args.count == 1, ParseInt("123") consumes the next register or Undefined instead of the provided argument, and IsFinite(42) can inspect Undefined and return false. Fix by centralizing these global builtins through one shared implementation with the correct argument base, and add regressions that exercise both mapped ID families 80-83 and 377-380 for single-argument and radix calls.

title: [10.7] Integrate `test262` ES2020 normative profile as a release blocker with explicit waiver file and zero silent failures policy.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.7 (Conformance + Verification), item 2.
Phase A exit gate: "ES2020 conformance gate: applicable test262 ES2020 normative profile passes with explicit zero-surprise waiver policy (waivers allowed only for documented non-normative harness/host gaps, never silent semantic failures)."
Related: 10.1 (feature-parity tracker), 10.2 (VM Core), 9A.1 (TS-first capability-typed IR execution).

## What
Integrate the official ECMA-402/test262 ES2020 normative test profile into FrankenEngine's CI pipeline as a hard release blocker, with an explicit machine-readable waiver file governing all non-passing tests and a zero-silent-failures enforcement policy.

## Detailed Requirements
1. **test262 checkout and pinning:** Pin a specific test262 commit hash in `conformance_pins.toml`. The pinned revision must cover the ES2020 normative profile (up to and including ES2020 features). Updates to the pin require a tracked bead and diff review.
2. **Profile selection:** Define an explicit test262 profile filter (`test262_profile.toml`) that includes all normative ES2020 tests and excludes: (a) tests for post-ES2020 proposals, (b) Annex B tests marked optional, (c) Intl/ECMA-402 tests (separate conformance track). Each exclusion must cite the normative clause justification.
3. **Harness implementation:** Implement test262 harness hooks (`$262.createRealm`, `$262.evalScript`, `$262.gc`, `$262.detachArrayBuffer`, `$DONE`, `print`, `assert.throws`, `assert.sameValue`, etc.) as a dedicated Rust module (`crate::test_harness::test262`). Hooks must faithfully implement ES2020 semantics without shortcuts.
4. **Waiver file (`conformance_waivers.toml`):** Shared with bd-d93. Each waiver entry requires: `test_id`, `reason_code` (enum: `harness_gap | host_hook_missing | intentional_divergence | not_yet_implemented`), `es2020_clause`, `tracking_bead`, `expiry_date`, `reviewer`. Waivers are reviewed monthly; expired waivers cause CI failure.
5. **Zero silent failures policy:** Any test262 test that is not explicitly (a) passing or (b) waived causes a hard CI gate failure. No "expected failure" lists, no "known flaky" suppression outside the waiver file.
6. **Parallel runner:** test262 contains ~45,000 tests. Runner must support parallel execution with deterministic scheduling (sorted test order, fixed worker assignment) so failures are reproducible.
7. **Structured reporting:** Emit per-test structured log: `trace_id`, `test_id`, `es2020_clause`, `outcome` (pass|fail|waived|timeout|crash), `duration_us`, `error_code`, `error_detail`. Aggregate into `test262_evidence.jsonl` with run manifest, profile hash, waiver file hash, and environment fingerprint.
8. **Release gate integration:** Wire the test262 gate into the release pipeline so that no release candidate can be cut while any unwaived test262 failure exists. Gate status is visible in the release checklist artifact.
9. **Regression tracking:** Maintain a monotonic pass-count high-water mark. Any commit that reduces the pass count (net of waiver changes) triggers a CI warning and requires explicit acknowledgment.

## Rationale
test262 is the industry-standard correctness oracle for ECMAScript engines. Without it as a release blocker, conformance claims are unverifiable. The waiver file makes the gap between current implementation and full conformance transparent and auditable. The zero-silent-failures policy ensures that conformance progress is monotonic and regressions are caught immediately, not discovered during release qualification.

## Testing Requirements (Meta-Tests for Test Infrastructure)
1. **Harness correctness meta-test:** Run a curated subset of test262 tests (>= 200, covering all harness hooks) against a known-good reference engine (e.g., V8 via d8) and confirm identical pass/fail classification.
2. **Waiver enforcement meta-test:** Inject a synthetic test that fails without a waiver entry and confirm CI blocks. Add a waiver and confirm CI passes. Remove the waiver and confirm CI blocks again.
3. **Expiry enforcement meta-test:** Set a waiver expiry to yesterday and confirm CI fails with a clear message identifying the expired waiver.
4. **Parallelism determinism meta-test:** Run the suite twice with the same seed and confirm identical test ordering and identical pass/fail sets.
5. **High-water-mark regression meta-test:** Simulate a commit that breaks a previously passing test without adding a waiver and confirm the regression warning fires.
6. **Profile filter meta-test:** Confirm the profile filter excludes exactly the intended test categories and includes no post-ES2020 tests.

## Implementation Notes
- test262 is checked out as a git submodule under `vendor/test262/` or fetched via a pinned archive URL.
- Runner binary: `franken_test262_runner` built as a separate binary target to avoid bloating the main engine binary.
- Waiver file path: `conformance/waivers/conformance_waivers.toml` (shared with bd-d93).
- Integration with `rch`-wrapped commands for heavy parallel test execution.
- The pass-count high-water mark is stored in `conformance/test262_hwm.json` and checked in to source control.

## Dependencies
- Upstream: 10.2 (VM Core must implement enough ES2020 semantics to run test262 tests), bd-d93 (shared waiver file and evidence format).
- Downstream: bd-2vu (lockstep suite references test262 pass/fail classification), 10.9 release gates (test262 conformance is a Phase A exit gate prerequisite).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.

title: [10.13] Add compile-time lint/CI guard rejecting ambient authority in extension-host control paths.
description:
# Add Compile-Time Lint/CI Guard Rejecting Ambient Authority

## Plan Reference
Section 10.13, Item 15.

## What
Implement a compile-time lint and/or CI guard that rejects any ambient authority usage in extension-host control paths. Every effectful operation must go through a `Cx`-gated API; direct access to global state, static resources, or implicit permissions is a hard compile/CI error.

## Detailed Requirements
- **Integration/binding nature**: The concept of ambient authority rejection is a 10.11 architectural principle. This bead integrates it as an enforced constraint in the FrankenEngine extension-host codebase via static analysis tooling.
- The lint/guard must detect:
  - Effectful function calls in extension-host modules that do not accept `Cx` as a parameter.
  - Direct use of `std::fs`, `std::net`, `std::process`, or any I/O API without `Cx`-gated wrappers.
  - Access to global/static mutable state (`static mut`, `lazy_static`, `once_cell` with mutable interior) in extension-host code.
  - Direct import from `franken_kernel`, `franken_decision`, or `franken_evidence` bypassing the adapter layer (bd-23om).
  - Definition of canonical types (`TraceId`, `DecisionId`, `PolicyId`, `SchemaVersion`, `Budget`, `Cx`) outside of `/dp/asupersync` crates (supporting bd-2fa1).
- Implementation options (choose based on Rust ecosystem maturity):
  - Custom clippy lint (preferred if feasible).
  - `cargo deny` rules for import-path violations.
  - Grep/regex-based CI check as a fallback (less reliable but immediately deployable).
  - Combination: regex-based check for immediate enforcement, custom clippy lint for long-term.
- The lint must run on every PR and block merge on violation.
- The lint must produce clear, actionable error messages explaining what the violation is and how to fix it (e.g., "Function `do_thing()` in extension-host module does not accept `Cx`. Add `cx: &Cx` as the first parameter.").

## Rationale
Ambient authority is the root cause of most privilege escalation and confused deputy attacks in extension systems. Manual code review catches some instances, but only static analysis catches them all. A compile-time lint ensures that the ambient authority prohibition is not just a policy but a mechanically-enforced invariant.

## Testing Requirements
- Positive test: write a compliant module (all effectful functions take Cx), verify the lint passes.
- Negative tests (one per violation type):
  - Function without Cx: verify lint failure.
  - Direct std::fs use: verify lint failure.
  - Static mutable state: verify lint failure.
  - Direct crate import bypassing adapter: verify lint failure.
  - Local type definition shadowing canonical type: verify lint failure.
- False positive test: verify the lint does not flag non-effectful functions (pure computations) that correctly omit Cx.
- Performance test: verify the lint completes in < 30 seconds on the full codebase.

## Implementation Notes
- **10.11 primitive ownership**: The ambient authority rejection principle and the Cx-based capability model are 10.11 architectural decisions. This bead mechanically enforces them in FrankenEngine's codebase.
- Start with the regex/grep-based check for immediate enforcement, then invest in a custom clippy lint for precision.
- The lint configuration should be stored in a well-known location (e.g., `.cargo/ambient_authority_lint.toml`) and documented.
- Coordinate with bd-2fa1 (no-fork policy enforcement can share lint infrastructure).

## Dependencies
- Depends on bd-2ygl (Cx threading must be in place before the lint can enforce Cx presence).
- Depends on bd-23om (adapter layer must exist before the lint can enforce adapter-only imports).
- No downstream dependencies; this is a cross-cutting enforcement mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.

title: [10.11] Build deterministic lab runtime harness with schedule replay, virtual time, and cancellation injection.
description:
## Plan Reference
- **Section**: 10.11 item 9 (FrankenSQLite-Inspired Runtime Systems Track)
- **9G Cross-ref**: 9G.4 — Deterministic lab runtime with interleaving exploration
- **Top-10 Links**: #3 (Deterministic evidence graph + replay), #9 (Adversarial security corpus)

## What
Build a deterministic lab runtime harness with schedule replay, virtual time, and cancellation injection. This harness replaces the standard async runtime in test/lab environments, providing full control over task scheduling, time progression, and fault injection so that concurrency-sensitive behaviors can be reproduced exactly.

## Detailed Requirements
1. Implement a \`LabRuntime\` that replaces the production async executor with a deterministic scheduler:
   - Tasks are scheduled by a deterministic policy (seed-driven permutation or explicit schedule script).
   - No real wall-clock time dependency: all time references use a \`VirtualClock\` that advances only when explicitly stepped or when the scheduler decides.
   - Random number generation uses seeded, reproducible RNG with transcript recording.
2. \`VirtualClock\` API:
   - \`advance(duration)\`: manually advance time.
   - \`advance_to_next_timer()\`: jump to the next pending timer/deadline.
   - \`now()\`: returns current virtual time.
   - All \`Duration\`-based APIs in the runtime must route through \`VirtualClock\` in lab mode.
3. Schedule replay: the harness records a \`ScheduleTranscript\` (ordered list of task-id executions, timer fires, and cancellation injections) and can replay it exactly.
4. Cancellation injection: the harness can inject cancellation signals at arbitrary points in the schedule (before/after specific task steps, at specific virtual times, at specific checkpoint sites from bd-3vg).
5. Fault injection: the harness supports injecting:
   - Task panics at specified points.
   - Channel disconnections.
   - Obligation leaks (for testing bd-qse).
   - Deadline expirations.
   - Region close requests at arbitrary times.
6. Determinism contract: given the same initial state, seed, and schedule transcript, the harness must produce byte-identical structured event sequences.
7. Output artifacts: the harness produces a \`LabRunResult\` bundle containing: schedule transcript, event log, virtual timeline, obligation audit, region state snapshots, and pass/fail verdict with failure diagnostics.
8. Integration with \`frankenlab\`: the harness must be compatible with the \`frankenlab\` scenario runner contract (Section 8.4.1) so that 10.13 can wire scenarios into release gates.

## Rationale
The 9G.4 contract requires that critical concurrency paths are tested via deterministic exploration, not probabilistic stress testing. Without a deterministic lab runtime, race conditions in cancellation/checkpoint/policy-update interactions are found only by luck. The schedule replay capability converts "it happened once in CI" into a reproducible, debuggable artifact. This directly supports the release-gate requirement (Section 8.4.3 invariant #6) that frankenlab scenarios are release blockers.

## Testing Requirements
- **Unit tests**: Verify \`VirtualClock\` advances correctly. Verify deterministic task ordering with fixed seed. Verify cancellation injection at specified points. Verify schedule transcript replay produces identical events.
- **Property tests**: Generate random schedules, run them, record transcripts, replay transcripts, and verify identical output.
- **Integration tests**: Run a multi-service scenario (policy controller + evidence flusher + extension cell) in the lab runtime, inject faults, and verify the supervision tree (bd-2gg) handles failures deterministically. Replay the transcript and verify identical behavior.
- **Regression tests**: Any previously-found concurrency bug should have a committed schedule transcript that serves as a regression test.
- **Logging/observability**: All lab runtime events carry virtual timestamps, task IDs, and injection markers for correlation.

## Implementation Notes
- Consider building on \`tokio-test\` or a custom single-threaded executor with explicit task-step control.
- \`VirtualClock\` should implement \`Clock\` trait that all runtime components use, with production impl routing to \`Instant::now()\` and lab impl routing to the virtual clock.
- Schedule transcript format should be a compact binary or JSONL format suitable for inclusion in CI artifacts and evidence bundles.
- The harness should support both scripted scenarios (explicit schedule) and exploratory mode (seed-driven random scheduling for the interleaving explorer bd-3ix).

## Dependencies
- Depends on: bd-3vg (checkpoint-placement provides injection points), bd-2ao (region-quiescence is exercised during fault injection), bd-1bl (obligation channels are tested under fault injection), bd-qse (lab-fatal policy enforcement).
- Blocks: bd-3ix (interleaving explorer uses the lab runtime), bd-yi6 (phase gates require lab runtime pass), 10.13 frankenlab scenario integration.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.

title: [10.11] Add bounded masking helper for tiny atomic publication steps only; block long-operation masking by policy.
description:
## Plan Reference
- **Section**: 10.11 item 5 (FrankenSQLite-Inspired Runtime Systems Track)
- **9G Cross-ref**: 9G.2 — Cancellation as protocol (request -> drain -> finalize)
- **Top-10 Links**: #3 (Deterministic evidence graph + replay)

## What
Add a bounded masking helper that allows tiny atomic publication steps to temporarily mask cancellation signals, with a strict policy that blocks long-operation masking. This ensures that critical atomic commit points (e.g., writing a finalized checkpoint, publishing an evidence entry, completing a two-phase commit) are not interrupted mid-operation while preventing abuse of masking to delay cancellation.

## Detailed Requirements
1. Define a \`CancelMask\` guard type that temporarily suppresses cancellation observation within a scoped block.
2. \`CancelMask\` must enforce a hard maximum duration bound (configurable, default 1ms) and a hard maximum instruction/operation count bound (configurable, default 64 operations).
3. If either bound is exceeded, the mask automatically drops and cancellation becomes observable. The violation is recorded as a \`MaskBoundExceeded\` evidence event with severity \`warning\` in production and \`fatal\` in lab mode.
4. \`CancelMask::new()\` requires a \`MaskJustification\` parameter containing: \`operation_name\`, \`expected_duration_hint\`, \`atomicity_reason\`.
5. Nesting of \`CancelMask\` is forbidden; attempting to create a nested mask must return \`MaskNestingDenied\` error.
6. Policy enforcement: a \`MaskPolicy\` configuration defines which operation names are allowed to mask and their per-operation bounds. Operations not in the allowlist cannot create masks.
7. All mask creation and release events must be recorded for replay determinism: \`trace_id\`, \`region_id\`, \`mask_id\`, \`operation_name\`, \`duration_actual\`, \`outcome\` (clean_release / bound_exceeded / cancel_deferred).

## Rationale
The 9G.2 cancellation protocol requires that cancellation is always observable, but some operations (atomic writes, hash-linked append, two-phase commit finalization) must complete atomically to avoid corruption. The bounded masking helper resolves this tension: it permits atomic completion while making it structurally impossible to abuse masking as a cancellation-avoidance mechanism. The hard bounds and policy allowlist prevent long operations from hiding behind masks, which would violate the \`<= 250ms\` containment SLO.

## Testing Requirements
- **Unit tests**: Verify mask correctly suppresses cancellation within bounds. Verify automatic drop on duration bound exceeded. Verify automatic drop on operation count exceeded. Verify nesting denial. Verify policy allowlist enforcement.
- **Property tests**: Fuzz mask durations and verify bound enforcement is never violated (mask never exceeds configured bounds by more than one check interval).
- **Integration tests**: Within a region-quiescence scenario (bd-2ao), create a mask during drain phase, verify atomic operation completes, then verify cancellation proceeds after mask release.
- **Lab mode test**: Verify that mask bound violation is fatal in lab mode (bd-121 harness).
- **Logging/observability**: Mask events carry structured fields for replay correlation and audit.
- **Reproducibility**: Mask timing must use virtual time in deterministic lab runtime for replay stability.

## Implementation Notes
- Implement as a RAII guard (\`Drop\` impl restores cancellation observability).
- Use thread-local or \`Cx\`-embedded state to track mask nesting depth and enforce the no-nesting rule.
- Duration bounds should be checked via monotonic clock (or virtual clock in lab mode), not wall clock.
- The \`MaskPolicy\` should be loadable from runtime configuration and updateable via policy epoch transitions (bd-xga).

## Dependencies
- Depends on: bd-2ao (region-quiescence protocol provides the cancellation flag that masks interact with), bd-3vg (checkpoint contract defines where masks are valid).
- Blocks: bd-1bl (obligation channels may use masks for atomic commit steps).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.

title: [review][react_ecosystem_compatibility] Include unresolved triage payloads in report hash
description: Review finding from commit 93390aed (feat(react_ecosystem_compatibility): add failure taxonomy, repro minimizer, and shipped-path classifier). The commit adds unresolved_failures with CompatibilityFailureTriage, MinimizedReactEcosystemRepro, owner_route, and ReactShippedPathClassification to crates/franken-engine/src/react_ecosystem_compatibility.rs, and the React package cohort bundle writes these reports to react_ecosystem_compat_report.json. However EcosystemCompatibilityReport::compute_hash at crates/franken-engine/src/react_ecosystem_compatibility.rs:688-706 still hashes only schema_version, security_epoch, each result.input_hash, passed bit, overall score, and gate_passed. It ignores result.errors, diagnostics, unresolved_failures, minimized repro fields, owner route, shipped-path classification, and execution/report metrics. As a result two reports can have the same report_hash while routing a React failure to different owners, emitting different failing_specifier values, or changing shipped_path_classification.reason/status, as long as the input pattern and pass/fail bit are unchanged. Existing hash tests only assert repeatability, not sensitivity to the newly added triage payload. Fix by adding length-prefixed/tagged hash input for the full deterministic triage payload (or a canonical JSON digest with report_hash excluded) and add regressions proving report_hash changes when failure_kind, failing_specifier, owner_route, classification status/reason, or errors change.
close_reason: done: hash the full deterministic ecosystem compatibility report payload, including unresolved triage details, and add regression coverage proving report_hash changes when triage/error fields change

## What
Publish governance scorecards covering attested-receipt coverage, privacy-budget health, moonshot-governor decisions, and cross-repo conformance stability as a unified operational health view.

## Detailed Requirements
1. Scorecard dimensions:
   - **Attested-receipt coverage**: percentage of high-impact decision receipts with valid non-expired attestation bindings (target: >= 95% per success criteria).
   - **Privacy-budget health**: current epoch budget consumption, burn rate, projected exhaustion, and any budget-overrun incidents (target: zero overruns).

title: [10.12] Add incident replay artifact bundle format and verifier CLI for external audit.
description:
## Plan Reference
- **10.12 Item 8** (Incident replay artifact bundle and verifier CLI)
- **9H.3**: Causal Time-Machine Runtime -> canonical owner: 9F.3 (Deterministic Time-Travel + Counterfactual Replay), execution: 10.12
- **9F.3**: Deterministic Time-Travel + Counterfactual Replay -- reproducible incident investigation for external audit

## What
Define the incident replay artifact bundle format and build a standalone verifier CLI that enables external auditors to independently reproduce and verify security incident investigations without trusting FrankenEngine runtime internals.

## Detailed Requirements

### Artifact Bundle Format
1. **Bundle contents**: A self-contained, portable archive containing:
   - Recorded deterministic trace(s) covering the incident window
   - Evidence ledger snapshot(s) at relevant decision points
   - Policy snapshot(s) active during the incident
   - All decision receipts (opt_receipt, containment receipts, fleet quorum checkpoints) within the incident scope
   - Nondeterminism log sufficient for bit-for-bit replay
   - Counterfactual analysis results (if performed)
   - Action delta reports comparing incident outcome vs alternative policies
   - Bundle manifest with content hash inventory, creation metadata, and chain-of-custody signatures
2. **Bundle integrity**: Content-addressed with Merkle tree over all constituent artifacts. Bundle signature by the producing node's signing key.
3. **Bundle versioning**: Schema version in manifest; verifier CLI supports at least current and N-1 bundle versions.
4. **Privacy controls**: Bundle redaction policy allows removal of sensitive data (tenant identifiers, payload contents) while preserving replay-relevant structure. Redacted fields are replaced with deterministic placeholders that maintain trace integrity.
5. **Bundle size management**: Configurable trace window (default: 5 minutes around incident trigger) and selective artifact inclusion. Compression support for storage efficiency.

### Verifier CLI
1. **Standalone binary**: Ships as a self-contained CLI tool (`franken-verify`) that does not require a running FrankenEngine instance or network access.
2. **Verification operations**:
   - `verify bundle <path>`: Check bundle integrity (Merkle tree, signatures, content hashes).
   - `verify replay <path>`: Re-execute traces from the bundle and verify bit-for-bit replay fidelity.
   - `verify receipts <path>`: Validate all decision receipt signature chains, transparency log proofs, and (optionally) attestation chains.
   - `verify counterfactual <path> --params <config>`: Re-run counterfactual analysis with auditor-specified parameters and compare against bundled results.
   - `inspect <path>`: Human-readable summary of bundle contents, timeline, decisions, and outcomes.
3. **Verification report**: Each verification operation emits a structured report (JSON + human-readable) with pass/fail per check, evidence of divergence if any, and confidence statement.
4. **Trust model**: Verifier trusts only the cryptographic primitives and its own replay logic. It verifies signatures against provided public keys (which may be independently obtained from transparency logs or key infrastructure).
5. **Deterministic execution**: Verifier replay produces identical results regardless of the host platform (modulo documented platform constraints).

### External Audit Workflow
1. Operator triggers bundle creation for a specific incident (manual or automatic on high-severity events).
2. Bundle is exported and delivered to external auditor via secure channel.
3. Auditor runs verifier CLI to independently validate all claims.
4. Auditor can run custom counterfactual analysis to test "what-if" scenarios.
5. Verification report serves as auditable evidence for governance, compliance, or legal proceedings.

## Rationale
> "Postmortems become experiments, not narratives." -- 9F.3
> "Security governance becomes auditable evidence, not trust-me logging. Operators, customers, and auditors can verify not only what happened but why and under which policy artifact." -- 9F.5

Incident replay bundles with independent verification are the mechanism that converts FrankenEngine's internal decision quality into externally defensible trust. This is essential for enterprise adoption and regulatory compliance.

## Testing Requirements
1. **Unit tests**: Bundle creation with all artifact types; Merkle tree construction and verification; redaction with integrity preservation; bundle versioning compatibility.
2. **CLI tests**: End-to-end CLI invocation for each verification operation on valid bundles, corrupted bundles, redacted bundles, and version-mismatched bundles.
3. **Replay fidelity tests**: Create bundle from live incident simulation; verify CLI replay produces identical outcomes on a clean host.
4. **Counterfactual tests**: Verify CLI counterfactual analysis with known alternate parameters produces expected action delta reports.
5. **Cross-platform tests**: Verify CLI replay determinism across Linux x86_64 and ARM64 (minimum supported platforms).
6. **Adversarial tests**: Tampered bundles (modified trace, swapped receipt, truncated evidence); verify CLI detects all corruption.

## Implementation Notes
- Bundle format: consider tar.zst or similar streaming archive with deterministic ordering for reproducible hashes.
- Verifier CLI should be a separate Rust binary with minimal dependencies (no runtime framework, no network stack).
- Replay logic in verifier should share core replay implementation with the runtime replay engine (bd-1nh) via a shared library crate, but with all external IO stubbed.
- Key distribution for signature verification is out of scope for this bead but must be documented (expected: transparency log integration or manual key pinning).

## Dependencies
- bd-1nh: Deterministic causal replay engine (provides replay logic and trace format)
- bd-yqe: Proof schema (receipt types in bundles)
- bd-du2: Fleet protocol messages (fleet evidence in bundles)
- 10.10: Cryptographic primitives, signature verification, audit chain format
- 10.5: Evidence ledger format, decision contract format

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.

title: [CRITICAL] [REVIEW] Deterministic replay coverage gap - execution paths lack replay witnesses
description:
Vision claim: '100% deterministic replay coverage for security-critical allow/deny/escalation decisions' (PLAN line 60) and 'Deterministic first, adaptive second' (README line 107).

Reality gap: Many execution paths in baseline_interpreter.rs and decision gates emit artifacts or make security decisions without replay witness generation. Examples:
- ArrayPush optimization (lines 4841+) - no replay witness for cache invalidation decisions
- Compromise-rate gate outcomes - decision artifacts emitted without replay coverage  
- Panic paths in baseline interpreter (lines 18510+) - error decisions not replay-captured
- Extension lifecycle events - emit without deterministic replay contracts

Impact: Security decisions cannot be forensically reconstructed, violating the core 'deterministic first' principle and making incident response impossible.

Required fix: Audit all decision/artifact emission paths and add mandatory replay witness generation for security-critical decisions. Every allow/deny/escalation must have deterministic replay coverage.

title: [10.15] Add frankensqlite-backed specialization index enabling deterministic audit queries from security proof -> optimization receipt -> benchmark outcome.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.15 (Delta Moonshots Execution Track), subsection 9I.8 (Security-Proof-Guided Specialization), item 4 of 4.

## What
Add a frankensqlite-backed specialization index enabling deterministic audit queries from security proof to optimization receipt to benchmark outcome.

## Detailed Requirements
1. Storage schema:
   - **Specialization receipts table**: stores proof_specialization_receipt artifacts indexed by receipt_id, proof_input_ids, optimization_class, extension_id (or slot_id), epoch_id, timestamp.
   - **Proof-to-specialization index**: given a proof_id, find all specializations it enables.
   - **Specialization-to-benchmark index**: given a specialization receipt_id, find associated benchmark results (performance delta measurements).
   - **Invalidation log**: records specialization invalidation events with reason (epoch change, proof expiry, proof revocation), timestamp, and fallback confirmation.
   - **Aggregate views**: per-extension specialization coverage, aggregate performance delta, proof utilization rates.
2. Deterministic audit queries:
   - Full audit chain: security_proof -> specialization_receipt -> benchmark_outcome, queryable in both directions.
   - Epoch-scoped queries: all specializations valid in a given epoch.
   - Invalidation queries: all specializations invalidated in a given time window with reasons.
3. Replay-join support: join specialization data with compilation logs, proof validation results, and benchmark runs.
4. Performance: audit chain queries must be bounded-latency with appropriate indexing.
5. All operations use /dp/frankensqlite integration patterns.

## Rationale
From 10.15: "Add frankensqlite-backed specialization index enabling deterministic audit queries from security proof -> optimization receipt -> benchmark outcome." The specialization index is the data substrate for: operator dashboards (specialization visibility), audit (proof-to-optimization traceability), and performance tracking (measuring the security-optimization flywheel effect). From success criteria: "100% of activated proof-specializations carry signed receipts linking security-proof inputs to transformation and rollback artifacts."

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: CRUD operations, index query correctness, audit chain traversal, replay joins.
- Conformance tests: deterministic retrieval, round-trip fidelity, schema migration.
- Performance tests: audit chain query latency at target data volumes.
- Integration tests: full specialization lifecycle with index population and audit queries.

## Implementation Notes
- Use /dp/frankensqlite; consider /dp/sqlmodel_rust for typed model layers.
- Audit chain is the primary query pattern; optimize index design accordingly.
- Consider materialized aggregate views for dashboard performance.

## Dependencies
- bd-6qsi (specialization receipt schema for stored data types).
- 10.6 (benchmark results for specialization-to-benchmark linkage).
- 10.14 (frankensqlite integration patterns).
- /dp/frankensqlite (storage framework).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Implement the full objective with deterministic behavior, explicit failure semantics, and safe fallback and rollback rules.
- Add focused unit tests for normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid and adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
- Add integration and end-to-end test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions, degraded mode, and recovery behavior with deterministic fixtures.
- Emit structured logs with stable keys (`trace_id`, `decision_id`, `policy_id`, `component`, `event`, `outcome`, `error_code`) and assert critical events in tests.
- Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, evidence pointers, replay pointers, benchmark/check outputs) plus clear operator verification steps.

title: extension-host binding session ids collide across extensions
description:
Round2 concurrency audit finding.

Evidence:
- ExtensionHostBinding::start_session accepts caller-provided session_id and inserts the session cell under that raw key at crates/franken-engine/src/execution_cell.rs:812 and crates/franken-engine/src/execution_cell.rs:836.
- CellManager::insert_cell rejects duplicate active keys at crates/franken-engine/src/execution_cell.rs:581 and crates/franken-engine/src/execution_cell.rs:587.
- The newer ExtensionHostLifecycleManager already avoids this by deriving deterministic extension-scoped IDs as {extension_id}::session::{session_id} at crates/franken-engine/src/extension_host_lifecycle.rs:643.

Two concurrently loaded extensions that both choose sess-1 collide in the shared manager. One session is rejected, and any lifecycle code that later addresses the raw session_id has no extension ownership boundary.

Fix: derive extension-scoped session cell IDs in ExtensionHostBinding, return/record the actual cell ID, and add a regression that ext-a/sess-1 and ext-b/sess-1 can coexist and unload independently.

title: [11] Define and enforce evidence-and-decision contract template for all subsystem proposals.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 11: Evidence And Decision Contracts (Mandatory)

## What
Create a mandatory contract template that every major subsystem proposal must satisfy before merge. The template enforces artifact-backed discipline across the entire program.

## Required Template Fields
Every proposal must include ALL of the following:
1. **Change summary**: What is being proposed and why
2. **Hotspot/threat evidence**: Profile data, threat model, or risk assessment justifying the change
3. **EV score and tier**: Expected value assessment using the program's EV >= 2.0 threshold from alien-graveyard methodology (Section 5.3)
4. **Expected-loss model**: Explicit loss matrix for the action space, following alien-artifact-coding discipline (Section 5.2)
5. **Fallback trigger**: Conditions under which the change auto-reverts or degrades to safe mode
6. **Rollout wedge**: Staged deployment strategy (shadow -> canary -> ramp -> default per Section 8.8)
7. **Rollback command**: Exact command(s) to revert the change
8. **Benchmark and correctness artifacts**: Before/after performance data, golden output checksums, test results

## Enforcement Rule
'No contract, no merge.' This is a hard gate, not a guideline.

## Rationale
From the plan's ambition-first doctrine: every claim must ship with proof artifacts. This contract template ensures that principle is operationalized at the PR level, preventing unfounded changes from entering the codebase.

## Testing Requirements
- Unit test: validate that a contract struct with any missing field fails validation
- Unit test: validate that a complete contract struct passes validation
- Integration test: CI gate that rejects PRs touching runtime code without a linked contract artifact
- Test that contract schema is versioned and backward-compatible

## Implementation Notes
- Implement as a Rust struct with serde support in a shared governance module
- Consider a CLI subcommand (frankenctl contract validate) for pre-commit checking
- Store validated contracts alongside code changes in a canonical location
- Reference: The extreme-software-optimization methodology (Section 5.1) mandates baseline/profile/prove/implement/verify for every optimization - this contract template is the enforcement mechanism

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid/adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end/integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds/fixtures and CI-ready command lines.

6. For Rust build/test workflows introduced by this bead, document/execute via `rch`-wrapped commands for heavy compilation/test workloads.

title: EPIC: Replace Homebrew Crypto with Standard Primitives
description:
CRITICAL FINDING (C3) from modes-of-reasoning analysis -- converged by 3 independent analytical modes (Deductive A1, Adversarial H2, Debiasing L2).

## Problem

The 3-tier hash strategy (IntegrityHash/ContentHash/AuthenticityHash) uses a hand-rolled SipHash-inspired construction instead of proven cryptographic primitives. This undermines the project's core security claims:

1. Tier 2/3 collapse: AuthenticityHash::compute(data) and ContentHash::compute(data) call the SAME collision_resistant_hash() function. The unkeyed AuthenticityHash is used in production paths (causal_replay.rs:595, proof_schema.rs:954,971). This breaks the claimed tier separation.

2. Non-collision-resistant hash: The collision-resistant hash is SipHash-inspired with only 2 mixing rounds per 8-byte block. SipHash is a PRF for hash table protection, NOT a collision-resistant hash function.

3. Symmetric MAC masquerading as signatures: sign_preimage() derives a verification key by hashing the signing key, then computes HMAC(vk, preimage). ANY verifier can forge signatures -- zero non-repudiation.

4. sha2 already a dependency: The sha2 crate is in Cargo.toml and used in ~20 files. The homebrew hash is used in 250+ call sites.

## Why This Matters

Every security-critical artifact -- capability tokens, evidence entries, decision receipts, policy checkpoints, epoch metadata -- flows through these hash/signature primitives. A third-party audit would immediately flag this.

## Key Files
- crates/franken-engine/src/hash_tiers.rs (280 dependents)
- crates/franken-engine/src/signature_preimage.rs
- crates/franken-engine/src/capability_token.rs
- crates/franken-engine/src/evidence_ledger.rs
- 250+ call sites using ContentHash::compute / AuthenticityHash::compute

## Success Criteria
- All Tier 2 hashing uses SHA-256 or BLAKE3
- All Tier 3 keyed hashing uses HMAC-SHA256
- Signature operations use Ed25519 asymmetric keys
- Unkeyed AuthenticityHash::compute removed from non-test code
- All tests pass, cargo check/clippy/fmt clean
close_reason: done: Completed crypto migration from homebrew primitives to standard cryptographic algorithms. All child beads completed: bd-13z5r.1 (ContentHash SHA-256), bd-13z5r.2 (AuthenticityHash HMAC-SHA256), bd-13z5r.3 (Ed25519 asymmetric signatures), bd-13z5r.4 (remaining call sites migration), bd-13z5r.5 (e2e test script). Replaced homebrew SipHash-inspired construction with SHA-256, symmetric MAC with HMAC-SHA256, and symmetric signature with Ed25519. All security-critical artifacts now use proven cryptographic primitives with proper non-repudiation and collision resistance.

title: Replace ContentHash collision_resistant_hash with SHA-256
description:
Replace the hand-rolled SipHash-inspired collision_resistant_hash() in hash_tiers.rs with SHA-256 (via the sha2 crate already in Cargo.toml).

## What to change
- hash_tiers.rs: Rewrite collision_resistant_hash() to use sha2::Sha256
- Keep the ContentHash newtype wrapper and all its API (compute, as_bytes, from_bytes, Display)
- Internal representation stays [u8; 32] -- SHA-256 output is 32 bytes, same as current
- Remove the custom 4xu64 state mixing logic

## Why SHA-256
- Already a dependency (sha2 in Cargo.toml)
- Proven collision resistance (unlike SipHash-inspired construction)
- Same output size (32 bytes) -- no structural changes
- Pure Rust, compatible with forbid(unsafe_code)

## Risk
- hash_tiers.rs has 280 dependents -- all recompile (but no API change)
- Test fixtures with hardcoded hash values need updating

## Files: crates/franken-engine/src/hash_tiers.rs (lines 80-130)

(c) Large input: compute(1MB of zeros) completes and matches. (d) Determinism: compute same input 1000x, all results identical. (e) Round-trip: ContentHash -> as_bytes -> from_bytes -> identical. (f) Display format: verify hex output matches SHA-256 convention. (g) BTreeMap ordering: insert ContentHash values, verify lexicographic order preserved. comments.text: PERFORMANCE CONSIDERATION: hash_tiers.rs has 280 dependents and ContentHash::compute is on the hot path for ALL content addressing. SHA-256 is ~3-5x slower than the current SipHash-inspired construction. Consider BLAKE3 instead: (a) blake3 crate is pure Rust, forbid(unsafe_code) compatible. (b) BLAKE3 is faster than SHA-256 and even faster than SipHash for large inputs. (c) BLAKE3 provides 256-bit collision resistance (same as SHA-256). (d) Single dependency (blake3 crate). RECOMMENDATION: Use BLAKE3 for ContentHash (Tier 2, performance-sensitive), HMAC-SHA256 for AuthenticityHash (Tier 3, security-critical), Ed25519 for signatures. This gives best performance on the hot path while using proven constructions everywhere.

title: Create crypto migration e2e test script with structured JSONL logging

title: [REVIEW][HIGH] Hostcall batch transport copies inline payloads into hash preimage buffers
description:
Finding: crates/franken-engine/src/hostcall_batch_transport.rs:783-817 computes each BatchEntry content hash by building a fresh Vec preimage and extending it with the full inline payload at line 795 before calling ContentHash::compute. The module advertises zero-copy payload transport, but inline hostcall batches pay an extra O(payload_bytes) memcpy and allocation solely for hashing. compute_batch_mac at crates/franken-engine/src/hostcall_batch_transport.rs:820-835 also builds a temporary Vec for every batch MAC, and submit_batch builds another receipt hash preimage at crates/franken-engine/src/hostcall_batch_transport.rs:1103-1113.

Why it matters: hostcall batching is a throughput path. For N inline entries totaling P bytes, content hashing currently copies P bytes into temporary buffers in addition to owning the payload Vecs in BatchPayload::Inline. That allocator/memcpy cost scales directly against the path meant to batch high-volume hostcalls; shared-region payloads avoid copying payload bytes, but inline batches still dominate small/medium-message workloads.

Measurable hypothesis: add chunked/streaming helpers for ContentHash and AuthenticityHash preimages, or a hostcall-local Sha256/HMAC builder that updates with domain separators, fixed-width fields, payload slices, and trace_id without materializing a Vec. On a fixture with 64 inline entries of 64 KiB each, expect >=45% reduction in allocation bytes and >=25% reduction in build_batch/entry-hash wall time, with byte-for-byte identical content_hash, batch_mac, receipt hash, corpus hashes, and evidence bundle output.

Validation plan: add focused equivalence tests comparing current vector-preimage outputs to the streaming implementation for Inline, SharedRegion, and Backpressure payloads; then run targeted hostcall_batch_transport unit/integration tests and corpus/evidence determinism checks. Keep deterministic replay artifacts unchanged; this is an implementation-path optimization only.

title: [10.15] Add governance audit ledger capturing all automatic and human override promote/hold/kill decisions with signed rationale.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.15 (Delta Moonshots Execution Track), subsection 9I.3 (Moonshot Portfolio Governor), item 3 of 3.

## What
Add a governance audit ledger that captures all automatic and human-override promote/hold/kill decisions for moonshot initiatives with signed rationale artifacts.

## Detailed Requirements
1. Ledger structure:
   - Append-only log of governance decision records.
   - Each record contains: `decision_id`, `moonshot_id`, `decision_type` (promote/hold/kill/pause/resume/override), `actor` (system or human identifier), `rationale` (structured justification), `scorecard_snapshot` (scoring state at decision time), `artifact_references` (evidence supporting the decision), `timestamp`, `signature`.
2. Automatic decisions: every governor-initiated transition must produce a ledger entry with the scoring engine's rationale (which criteria passed/failed, metric values, confidence levels).
3. Human override decisions: must include signed justification explaining why the automatic recommendation was overridden, with explicit acknowledgment of any risk criteria being bypassed.
4. Ledger integrity:
   - Chained hashing (each entry includes hash of previous entry) for tamper evidence.
   - Periodic signed checkpoints for efficient consistency verification.
   - Compatible with transparency-log verification patterns.
5. Query interface: support queries by moonshot, decision type, actor, time range, and override status.
6. Governance reporting: support aggregate queries for governance scorecards (override frequency, kill rate, time-to-decision, portfolio health trends).

## Rationale
From 9I.3: "Human override remains available but must emit signed justification artifacts so governance drift is auditable." and "Kill-switch and pause semantics are first-class: initiatives that consume budget without signal, violate risk constraints, or fail reproducibility gates are automatically demoted or terminated." The audit ledger ensures that both automatic and manual governance decisions create an auditable, tamper-evident record that supports accountability and organizational learning.

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: record creation, chain-hash verification, checkpoint generation, query correctness for each filter dimension.
- Integration tests: full decision lifecycle with automatic and override entries, verify ledger integrity across multiple decisions, verify query API returns correct results.
- Adversarial tests: attempt to insert records out of order, tamper with chain hashes, forge override justifications.
- Performance tests: ledger append and query performance under realistic decision volumes.

## Implementation Notes
- Use frankensqlite for ledger persistence with appropriate indexing for query patterns.
- Chain-hash scheme should be compatible with the transparency-log patterns used elsewhere (9I.1, PLAS).
- Override frequency metrics should feed the governance scorecards (bd-12n5).

## Dependencies
- bd-3ncx (moonshot contract schema for moonshot identifiers and decision types).
- bd-1fu7 (scoring engine that generates automatic decisions).
- frankensqlite integration for persistence.
- 10.10 (deterministic serialization for ledger records).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.

title: [HIGH] [REVIEW] Capability WitnessValidator omits signature and promotion checks
description:
Reality-check scope: capability_witness.rs validation surface versus signed capability_witness guarantees.

capability_witness.rs:1494-1512 documents WitnessValidator as validating capability witness artifacts and says validate() is Full validation of a witness artifact. The broader docs describe signed capability_witness artifacts and promoted snapshots as the security boundary for PLAS.

The implementation at capability_witness.rs:1513-1561 checks schema compatibility, non-empty required capabilities, proof coverage, content-hash integrity, and confidence threshold. It does not verify synthesizer signatures, trusted signer identity, promotion signatures/quorum, lifecycle-state requirements, promotion theorem gate status, rollback token validity, or denial-record coverage. Tests such as crates/franken-engine/tests/capability_witness.rs:996-1001 treat this validator as passing a valid witness before promotion checks run.

Impact: any caller that treats WitnessValidator::validate as full artifact validation can accept a witness that is unsigned/untrusted or not promotion-safe, weakening the signed least-authority artifact boundary. Even if active acceptance performs extra checks, the module exposes a misleading validation API for security-sensitive artifacts.

Acceptance: split the API into explicit structural validation vs trust/promotion validation, or make WitnessValidator::validate perform the full trust-chain, signature/quorum, theorem-report, lifecycle, and rollback checks required before a witness can be used as a security decision input.
close_reason: shipped: WitnessValidator now separates structural validation from signed security-decision validation, with trust-root synthesizer verification, promotion quorum/theorem checks, promoted lifecycle requirement, rollback token shape checks, and denial-record coverage. title: [10.2] Define proof-to-specialization linkage in IR contracts (`proof_input_ids`, `optimization_class`, `validity_epoch`, `rollback_token`) for IR3/IR4 artifacts.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.2, item 6. Cross-refs: 9I.8 (Security-Proof-Guided Specialization), 9F.1 (Verified Adaptive Compiler), 10.12 (proof schema for optimizer), 10.15 (specialization receipt schema).

## What
Define the linkage between security proofs and optimizer specializations in IR3/IR4 artifacts. This enables security proofs to serve as optimizer inputs, so tighter verified constraints yield faster executable paths.

## Detailed Requirements
- IR3 artifacts must carry: proof_input_ids (which proofs justify this specialization), optimization_class (superinstruction, trace specialization, layout specialization, devirtualized hostcall fast paths), validity_epoch (when this specialization expires), rollback_token (how to revert to unspecialized path)
- IR4 witness artifacts must record: which specializations were active during execution, what proofs were consumed, performance delta observed
- Specializations must be invalidated deterministically on policy/proof epoch changes (per 9I.8)
- Automatic fallback to unspecialized baseline paths when proofs expire or are invalidated

## Rationale
Section 9I.8: 'Make security proofs first-class optimizer inputs so tighter verified constraints yield faster executable paths instead of being treated as overhead.' This creates a structural flywheel: better security → better proofs → faster code → more security investment justified. This is described as 'a structural flywheel unavailable to generic runtimes without proof-bearing security planes.'

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: IR3 artifacts with proof linkage serialize/deserialize correctly
- Unit tests: specialization invalidation on epoch change triggers rollback
- Unit tests: fallback path produces semantically identical results to specialized path
- Specialization-conformance suite (10.7): proof-specialized and unspecialized execution remain semantically equivalent

## Dependencies

title: [10.10] Add optional threshold-signing workflow for emergency revocation and key rotation operations.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.10, item 13. Cross-refs: 9E.5 (Key-role separation plus owner-signed attestation lifecycle - "Add optional threshold owner signing for high-impact operations (rotations/revocations) to reduce single-key compromise blast radius"), Top-10 links #5, #10.

## What
Add an optional threshold-signing workflow for emergency operations such as key revocation and key rotation. Instead of requiring a single owner key to authorize these high-impact actions, a threshold scheme requires k-of-n key shares to co-sign, ensuring that no single compromised key can unilaterally rotate keys or revoke critical credentials.

## Detailed Requirements
- Implement threshold signature scheme: support k-of-n threshold (e.g., 2-of-3, 3-of-5) where k shares must cooperate to produce a valid signature
- Threshold scheme selection: use Shamir-based threshold ECDSA/EdDSA or FROST (Flexible Round-Optimized Schnorr Threshold signatures) for Ed25519 compatibility
- Define `ThresholdSigningPolicy` object: `threshold_k: u32`, `total_n: u32`, `authorized_shares: Vec<ShareHolderId>`, `policy_id: EngineObjectId`
- Scope of threshold operations: emergency key revocation, key rotation, authority set changes (epoch transitions), and checkpoint creation for high-severity policy changes
- Non-threshold operations: regular signing, encryption, and token issuance remain single-key for performance (threshold is only for emergency/administrative operations)
- Share distribution ceremony: provide a deterministic, auditable workflow for initial share generation and distribution
- Share refresh: support proactive share refresh (re-sharing without changing the public key) to limit exposure from share compromise
- Partial signature collection: implement a coordinator-free protocol where partial signatures are submitted independently and combined when threshold is reached
- Audit: every threshold operation must emit a structured audit event identifying which shares participated
- Degraded mode: if fewer than k shares are available, the operation fails with `InsufficientThresholdShares` error; no fallback to single-key

## Rationale
From plan section 9E.5: "Add optional threshold owner signing for high-impact operations (rotations/revocations) to reduce single-key compromise blast radius. This mirrors FCP's identity hygiene in a runtime-centric model." Emergency operations like key revocation and rotation are the most sensitive actions in the system. If a single owner key is compromised, an attacker could revoke legitimate keys or rotate to attacker-controlled keys, effectively taking over the principal. Threshold signing ensures that these operations require cooperation of multiple parties, making such attacks require compromising k independent keys simultaneously -- exponentially harder than compromising one.

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: generate k-of-n threshold key shares, verify combined signature is valid
- Unit tests: verify k-1 shares cannot produce a valid signature
- Unit tests: verify k shares from different subsets all produce valid signatures
- Unit tests: verify share refresh produces new shares that are compatible with the same public key
- Unit tests: verify threshold policy enforcement (only threshold-scoped operations require threshold)
- Unit tests: verify InsufficientThresholdShares error when below threshold
- Unit tests: verify audit event emission with participating share identifiers
- Integration tests: multi-party threshold signing ceremony for key revocation
- Integration tests: threshold signing for epoch transition (authority set change)
- Integration tests: share distribution ceremony with deterministic verification
- Adversarial tests: attempt emergency operation with single share, verify rejection

## Implementation Notes
- FROST is the recommended threshold scheme for Ed25519 compatibility; consider using the `frost-ed25519` crate as a foundation
- The coordinator-free approach avoids a single point of failure in threshold signing; partial signatures can be collected via the existing session channel (bd-1bi)
- Share storage is critical: each share holder must protect their share with at least the same rigor as a full private key
- The threshold policy should be stored in the PolicyCheckpoint (bd-1c7) so that threshold requirements are themselves protected by the checkpoint chain
- This is an optional module; the system must function correctly with single-key signing when threshold is not configured

## Dependencies
- Depends on: bd-3ai (key role separation for understanding which operations are threshold-scoped), bd-1dp (key attestation for threshold share attestation), bd-1b2 (signature preimage contract for threshold signature output format)
- Blocks: bd-26o (conformance suite tests threshold signing), bd-1c7 (PolicyCheckpoint may use threshold signatures for high-severity changes)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Implement the full objective with deterministic behavior, explicit failure semantics, and safe fallback/rollback rules.
- Add focused unit tests for normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
- Add integration and/or end-to-end test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions, degraded mode, and recovery behavior with deterministic fixtures.
- Emit structured logs with stable keys (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and assert critical events in tests.
- Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, evidence pointers, replay pointers, benchmark/check outputs) plus clear operator verification steps.
- Ensure heavy Rust build/test execution paths are documented and run through rch wrappers when implementation begins.
