title: [PSRP-10] User-Facing Parser Excellence (Diagnostics, Recovery, Ergonomics)
description:
## Context
Mission: ensure the parser is not only fast/correct, but materially better for users through clearer diagnostics, robust recovery behavior, and ergonomic/stable integration surfaces.

Why this matters:
- Users experience parser quality through error messages, resilience after malformed code, and API usability.
- A parser can win microbenchmarks yet still fail real developer workflows if diagnostics and recovery are weak.

Scope and intent:
- Establish a diagnostics quality rubric and enforce it with golden tests.
- Improve error recovery/resynchronization so downstream tooling gets useful partial structure.
- Harden parser APIs/contracts and migration ergonomics for consumers.
- Publish operator/developer runbooks that make replay and troubleshooting straightforward.

## Acceptance Criteria
See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.

## Success Criteria
See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Diagnostics quality rubric (clarity, location accuracy, fix hint usefulness, determinism) is codified and test-enforced.
2. Recovery/resynchronization behavior passes adversarial e2e scenarios while preserving deterministic semantics and safety.
3. Parser APIs are versioned, documented, compatibility-tested, and accompanied by migration guidance where needed.
4. Operator/developer runbooks provide deterministic troubleshooting workflows with rich logs and replay commands.
5. User-impact metrics (diagnostic quality and recovery success rates) are tracked and referenced in PSRP-08 evidence bundles.
6. User-facing quality is backed by both focused unit tests and end-to-end workflow scripts.

title: [PSRP-02] Differential Parser Lab (Boa + Peer Parsers) and Drift Intelligence
description:
## Context
Mission: establish a standing oracle that continuously compares FrankenEngine parser behavior against external parsers and classifies divergences deterministically.

Why this matters:
- If we cannot measure where we differ from mature parsers, we cannot make credible correctness claims.
- Differential testing yields high-signal bug discovery and prevents local overfitting.
- A structured drift taxonomy lets us prioritize semantic correctness work instead of chasing noise.

Scope and intent:
- Build a repeatable harness across FrankenEngine, Boa, and at least one additional parser implementation.
- Normalize parser outputs into comparable forms (AST shape, token stream, diagnostics envelope).
- Auto-classify divergences (critical semantic mismatch vs benign representational difference).
- Continuously feed minimized counterexamples into parser, lexer, and IR workstreams.

Design constraints:
- Deterministic replay must be available for every discovered divergence.
- Classification rules must be versioned and reviewable.
- Comparison artifacts should be machine-consumable and human-auditable.

## Acceptance Criteria
See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.

## Success Criteria
See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Differential harness runs deterministic FrankenEngine-vs-Boa-vs-peer comparison over curated + generated corpora.
2. Output normalization adapters reduce false-positive drift and are covered by adapter unit/property tests.
3. Divergence classifier emits severity, candidate owner, replay command, and structured logs suitable for automation.
4. Scheduled differential e2e jobs publish trend reports and minimized repro artifacts with retained provenance.
5. New critical divergences automatically open/update remediation beads with test fixtures and deterministic replay metadata.
close_reason: All PSRP-02 child beads are closed with deterministic artifact-backed evidence; differential harness + drift intelligence scope is complete.

title: [PSRP-05] Parallel Deterministic Parsing Engine
description:
## Context
Mission: deliver true parallel parsing speedups with provable deterministic behavior and robust serial fallback.

Why this matters:
- Parallelism is mandatory for top-tier throughput on large sources.
- Without deterministic scheduler/merge proofs, parallel gains are operationally unsafe.

Intent:
- Achieve parallel speedups without introducing replay ambiguity or user-visible instability.

## Acceptance Criteria
See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.

## Success Criteria
See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Partitioning, scheduling, and merge witnesses are deterministic across seeds/runs.
2. Timeout/cancellation/backpressure behavior is deterministic and tested with adversarial scenarios.
3. Serial fallback triggers are explicit, replayable, and exercised in e2e flows.
4. Worker-count parity matrix is green before promotion.
5. Scheduler/merge logs are structured and sufficient for independent replay/debug.
6. Unit tests for partition/schedule/merge primitives and e2e deterministic stress scripts are both mandatory.

Validation: rustfmt check passes locally; rch targeted integration test log_entries_include_cancellation_and_backpressure_fields passed. Additional rch runs are in-flight/slow due shared worker contention and repeated repo_updater --format incompat warnings during sync.

comments.text: Fresh-eyes audit pass on the parallel parser core found and fixed two concrete defects in the reserved slice. 1) UTF-8-unsafe chunk splitting: compute_chunk_plan() could over-commit worker_count relative to usable safe split points and then fall back to arbitrary byte offsets via max_end, while parse() silently converted invalid UTF-8 chunk slices with from_utf8(...).unwrap_or(""). Fix: only count boundaries strictly before end-of-input as usable split points, cap worker_count to usable_boundaries + 1, fail closed to a single chunk if no safe boundary can be selected, and surface invalid UTF-8 chunk splits as ParseError::LexerError instead of silently dropping bytes. 2) FlakeRate contract bug: FlakeRate::compute() could emit rate_millionths > 1_000_000 even though the type documents 1_000_000 = 100%. Fix: clamp mismatched_runs to total_runs before computing rate/threshold verdicts. Added focused regressions in parallel_parser_integration.rs and parallel_interference_gate_integration.rs. Verification: targeted rch no-run compile passed for  using CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/tmp/rch_target_franken_engine_parallel_audit on worker vmi1227854. title: [PSRP-08] Supremacy Readiness Gate (Correctness + Performance + Determinism)
description:
## Context
Mission: define and enforce the final evidence bar before any world-leading parser claim is accepted.

Why this matters:
- This closes the gap between engineering progress and claim integrity.
- It prevents premature declaration without full, reproducible proof.

Intent:
- Fail closed unless correctness, performance, reproducibility, testing rigor, and user-facing quality all meet contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.

## Success Criteria
See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Supremacy criteria and mandatory evidence package are explicit and machine-checkable.
2. Correctness gate requires zero unresolved high-severity differential drifts.
3. Performance gate requires threshold wins versus Boa/peers on declared quantiles/workloads.
4. Comprehensive unit/property/regression/e2e suites with structured logs are green and linked.
5. User-facing quality signals (diagnostics and recovery) meet published thresholds.
6. Final readiness report includes risk register, rollback posture, and third-party rerun evidence.

title: [PSRP-08.1] Define supremacy criteria and mandatory evidence contract
description:
## Context
Define the supremacy contract early, then keep it versioned and machine-evaluable as implementation evidence accumulates.

Intent:
- Publish an initial criteria contract early enough to guide implementation decisions.
- Make criteria updates explicit, auditable, and diffable rather than implicit scope drift.
- Ensure the gate can be executed automatically from artifact bundles.

See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A versioned supremacy criteria spec (v0+) is published before downstream gate closure and covers correctness, determinism, performance, reproducibility, verification rigor, and user-facing quality.
2. Criteria are machine-checkable via an automated evaluator with focused unit tests for each rule class.
3. A deterministic e2e gate simulation validates evaluator behavior against representative artifact bundles.
4. Criteria changes require logged rationale, impact assessment, and compatibility notes in a criteria changelog.
5. Structured gate logs include: `run_id`, `criteria_version`, `git_sha`, `artifact_bundle_id`, `verdict`, and replay command.

Required verification addendum: include focused unit tests and, for any cross-subsystem behavior, deterministic e2e scenarios with structured logs/traces and one-command replay instructions.

Picked up stale-open PSRP-08.3 and hardened `scripts/run_parser_performance_promotion_gate.sh` so interrupted/stale `rch` paths classify fail-closed instead of collapsing to a generic failed command.

Changes:
- added ANSI-stripping before `rch` log parsing
- classify non-recoverable failures as `(rch-exit=<code>)`, `(remote-exit=<code>)`, `(timeout-<N>s)`, and `(missing-remote-exit-marker)`
- extended focused contract test + doc wording to require the new operator-facing semantics

Verification (all heavy cargo via `rch`):
- `./scripts/run_parser_performance_promotion_gate.sh ci` produced `artifacts/parser_performance_promotion_gate/20260321T235024Z/run_manifest.json`; `check` passed, `test` reproduced stale-progress and after cancellation the manifest now records `failed_command = cargo test -p frankenengine-engine --test parser_performance_promotion_gate (rch-exit=15)`
- `./scripts/run_parser_performance_promotion_gate.sh clippy` passed with `artifacts/parser_performance_promotion_gate/20260321T235852Z/run_manifest.json`
- `cargo fmt --check` via `rch` failed, but only on pre-existing/unrelated formatting drift in `crates/franken-engine/src/bin/franken_signature_drift_gate.rs` and `crates/franken-engine/tests/queueing_admission_control_deep_integration.rs`
- repo-wide `cargo check --all-targets` via `rch` (`target_rch_sunnydog_alltargets`) made workspace compile progress, then hit remote stale-progress and was manually cancelled; recent build id `29750734287276106`, exit `130`

Reserved files touched only:
- scripts/run_parser_performance_promotion_gate.sh
- crates/franken-engine/tests/parser_performance_promotion_gate.rs
- docs/PARSER_PERFORMANCE_PROMOTION_GATE.md

title: [PSRP-08.4] Final readiness report, risk register, and rollback posture
description:
## Context
Produce the final readiness dossier that synthesizes technical evidence, user impact, residual risk, and rollback posture before any supremacy declaration.

Intent:
- Make the final decision legible to future operators without reconstructing tribal context.
- Preserve a clear rollback and contingency path if post-declaration evidence regresses.

## Acceptance Criteria
See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Final dossier links all upstream correctness/performance/reproducibility/testing/user-quality evidence with immutable artifact references.
2. Residual risks are ranked with owners, mitigations, and trigger thresholds.
3. Rollback posture defines explicit triggers, blast-radius assumptions, and deterministic recovery scripts.
4. Independent verification outcomes and operator runbook validation are attached and signed off.
5. Final declaration package includes deterministic replay commands for each major claim.

Required verification addendum: include focused unit tests and, for any cross-subsystem behavior, deterministic e2e scenarios with structured logs/traces and one-command replay instructions.
close_reason: Hardened parser final readiness dossier fixture preflight to fail closed on schema/log-schema/bead-id mismatches; added regression assertions and verified focused test, fmt, check, and clippy gates.

title: [PSRP-09] Verification Matrix, Test Pyramid, and Evidence Logging Hardening
description:
## Context
Mission: make parser quality measurable and enforceable through a full verification pyramid that includes unit, property, regression, and end-to-end validation with deterministic evidence logs.

Why this matters:
- Architecture and performance work can regress correctness unless guarded by deep test coverage.
- E2E scripts with rich logging are the fastest way to root-cause failures across parser, lexer, event IR, and parallel scheduler layers.
- Claims of world-leading reliability require auditable proof artifacts, not just green local runs.

Scope and intent:
- Define verification architecture and quantitative coverage goals per parser subsystem.
- Build comprehensive unit/property/regression suites tied to drift categories.
- Implement deterministic e2e scripts that emit structured logs, replay manifests, and diff-friendly artifacts.
- Enforce CI quality gates and long-horizon artifact retention so regressions are explainable weeks later.

## Acceptance Criteria
See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.

## Success Criteria
See acceptance criteria field for explicit completion gates.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Verification architecture documents a test pyramid with explicit coverage targets for lexer, parser, event IR, parallel scheduler/merge, diagnostics, and API boundaries.
2. Every subsystem has comprehensive unit + property + regression tests with deterministic fixtures and reproducible failure minimization.
3. E2E scenario harness covers success, malformed input, adversarial input, cancellation, timeout, and fallback paths with structured run logs.
4. CI gates fail closed on missing coverage/quality thresholds and retain enough artifacts/logs for replay-based triage.
5. Test and e2e evidence is linked into PSRP-08 readiness gating without manual reconstruction.
close_reason: All PSRP-09 child beads closed with deterministic evidence lanes

## What

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Detailed Implementation Requirements

### Charter Document Structure
The runtime charter (docs/RUNTIME_CHARTER.md) must codify the following non-negotiable constraints from Section 4:

1. **Native-Only Execution Policy**: FrankenEngine owns parser-to-scheduler semantics in Rust. No rusty_v8, rquickjs, or equivalent binding-led core execution path. The engine is NOT a wrapper around V8 or QuickJS — it is a de novo implementation inspired by their semantics.

2. **Legacy Corpora Policy**: legacy_quickjs/ and legacy_v8/ directories are reference corpora only. They exist for semantic harvesting (understanding observable behavior, edge cases, compatibility-critical semantics) but NEVER as execution substrates. No code from these directories may be compiled into production binaries.

3. **Adaptive Systems Constraint**: Any adaptive or learning system (e.g., the Bayesian guardplane's posterior updates, regime detection, VOI-budgeted monitoring) MUST have a deterministic safe-mode fallback. If the adaptive component fails or produces untrusted output, the system degrades to a known-good deterministic path. This is the 'deterministic first, adaptive second' principle.

4. **Evidence-First Claims**: Every significant published claim (performance benchmarks, security improvements, compatibility coverage) requires reproducible evidence artifacts. No artifact, no claim. This applies to README badges, blog posts, conference presentations, and any external communication.

5. **Repository Split Contract**: /dp/franken_engine is the canonical engine repo. /dp/franken_node is the compatibility/product repo. Dependency direction is one-way: franken_node depends on franken_engine, never the reverse. No forked engine crates inside franken_node.

6. **Sibling Reuse Policy**: TUI surfaces use /dp/frankentui. SQLite persistence uses /dp/frankensqlite. Service/API control surfaces prefer /dp/fastapi_rust. No parallel local replacements without explicit approval.

### Document Format
- Markdown with clear section headers matching each constraint
- Each constraint must include: rule statement, rationale, enforcement mechanism, violation response
- Machine-parseable metadata section for CI lint consumption
- Version-controlled with change-log tracking charter amendments

### CI Integration
- Pre-commit or CI lint job verifies:
  - docs/RUNTIME_CHARTER.md exists and is non-empty
  - All Section 4 constraint keywords appear in the document
  - AGENTS.md references the charter location
  - No production Cargo.toml lists rusty_v8, rquickjs, or similar binding crates

## Rationale
This is the foundational governance document. Every architecture decision, every code review, every bead acceptance gate references back to this charter. Without it, the non-negotiable constraints are aspirational plan text rather than enforceable policy. Making it a CI-checked document ensures it cannot be silently violated.

## Testing Requirements
- Document existence and completeness CI lint
- Cross-reference check: AGENTS.md mentions charter path
- Negative test: verify Cargo.toml dependency scanner would flag binding crates
- Structured log: charter validation emits pass/fail event with constraint_id for each rule

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Detailed Implementation Requirements

### Claim Language Policy Structure
This policy document defines the rules for all published runtime claims. It bridges Section 11 (Evidence and Decision Contracts) and Section 14 (Benchmark Standard).

### Mandatory Claim Classes
1. **Performance Claims**: Any claim about speed, throughput, latency, memory usage, or efficiency.
   - Required evidence: reproducible benchmark artifact bundle (env.json, manifest.json, repro.lock per the reproducibility contract)
   - Required format: median + p95 + p99 with confidence intervals, workload description, hardware specification
   - Forbidden: unqualified superlatives ('fastest', 'best') without comparative methodology

2. **Security Claims**: Any claim about attack surface reduction, containment capability, threat mitigation, or trust model properties.
   - Required evidence: formal or semi-formal argument with test coverage, adversarial corpus results, and reproducible attack scenario demonstrations
   - Required format: threat model scope, attack vector catalog, tested/untested boundary declaration

3. **Compatibility Claims**: Any claim about Node.js API coverage, test262 pass rate, or ecosystem library support.
   - Required evidence: lockstep differential test results, test262 subset pass rates, compatibility matrix with specific version ranges
   - Required format: tested surface enumeration, known gap/waiver list, regression test evidence

4. **Determinism Claims**: Any claim about replay fidelity, bit-stability, or reproducibility.
   - Required evidence: replay transcript artifacts, cross-platform verification, seed/transcript pairs
   - Required format: conditions under which determinism holds, known non-deterministic boundaries

### Allowed Verbs and Quantifiers
- Allowed: 'provides', 'achieves', 'targets', 'measured at', 'demonstrated'
- Quantifiers must include units, conditions, and confidence: '3.2x median throughput improvement on extension-heavy workloads (95% CI: 2.8x-3.6x, n=1000, workload: mixed-compute)'
- Forbidden: 'revolutionary', 'unmatched', 'impossible to', 'guaranteed' (unless mathematically provable)

### Evidence Bundle Structure
Each claim must link to a reproducibility bundle containing:
- env.json: hardware, OS, toolchain versions
- manifest.json: test/benchmark configuration, seed values
- repro.lock: pinned dependency versions
- results/: raw output files
- verify.sh: one-command reproduction script

### Review/Approval Gates
- Claims in README: require at least one reproducibility bundle link
- Claims in external communication: require reviewer sign-off + bundle verification
- Claims in benchmarks: require third-party reproducibility instructions

### Violation Handling
- Claims found without evidence: immediate retraction or suspension pending evidence generation
- Claims found with stale evidence: grace period for re-verification, then retraction
- Repeated violations: escalation to charter review

## Rationale
The plan's evidence-first philosophy (Section 11) requires that no claim ships without artifacts. This policy makes that enforceable and consistent across all communication. It prevents the credibility erosion that comes from unsupported marketing claims and ensures FrankenEngine's public posture is always backed by reproducible evidence.

## Testing Requirements
- Policy document review: all claim classes defined
- Integration test: mock claim publication pipeline rejects claims without evidence bundles
- Structured logging: claim validation events emit claim_class, evidence_status, reviewer, outcome

title: [10.1] Add reproducibility contract (env.json, manifest.json, repro.lock) template
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.1 (Charter + Governance), item 3. Cross-refs: 7.5 (Fairness + Reproducibility Rules), 11 (Evidence And Decision Contracts), 14.3 (Reproducibility + Neutral Verification).

## What
Create a canonical reproducibility contract template that every benchmark result, performance claim, security claim, and published artifact must include. This template defines three required files: `env.json` (hardware/OS/runtime envelope), `manifest.json` (run parameters, dataset checksums, seed transcripts, harness commit IDs), and `repro.lock` (deterministic lockfile for exact reproduction).

## Detailed Requirements
1. **env.json schema**: Must capture hardware (CPU model, core count, cache sizes, RAM), OS (kernel version, distribution), runtime versions (Rust toolchain, franken_engine commit, baseline Node/Bun versions), environment variables that affect behavior, and timestamp/timezone.
2. **manifest.json schema**: Must capture run ID, benchmark suite version, workload parameters, dataset checksums (SHA-256), random seed transcripts, CLI flags, warmup/cooldown protocols, and harness commit ID (exact git SHA).
3. **repro.lock schema**: Must capture Cargo.lock hash, pinned dependency versions, feature flags, compilation profile, and target architecture so that `cargo build` from the lockfile produces bitwise-identical binaries.
4. All three files must use deterministic JSON serialization (sorted keys, no optional whitespace) so their content hashes are stable across machines.
5. A `validate_repro_contract()` function must check that all required fields are present and well-formed, producing structured error messages for any missing or invalid field.
6. Template files must be committed to the repository as reference examples under `docs/reproducibility/`.
7. The contract must be extensible (additional optional fields allowed) but the required field set must be stable across versions with explicit deprecation policy.

## Rationale
Section 7.5 of the plan mandates that all benchmark runs use identical hardware/OS envelopes, dataset seeds, and harness versions, with full run manifests committed alongside results. Section 11 requires every subsystem proposal to include benchmark and correctness artifacts. Section 14.3 requires one-command neutral verifier mode. Without a standardized reproducibility contract, these requirements cannot be enforced consistently. This template is the foundation for all reproducibility infrastructure.

## Testing Requirements
- **Unit tests**: Validate schema parsing for all three file types. Test with valid examples, missing required fields, extra optional fields, invalid types, and empty files.
- **Round-trip tests**: Generate a contract from current system state, serialize to JSON, deserialize, re-serialize, and verify bitwise equality (deterministic serialization proof).
- **Integration test**: Run a minimal benchmark, generate the three contract files automatically, then use them to reproduce the run on the same machine and verify identical outputs.
- **Adversarial tests**: Malformed JSON, extremely large field values, missing checksums, conflicting version fields.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All three schema files are defined with typed Rust structs using serde Serialize/Deserialize.
- `validate_repro_contract()` passes on well-formed inputs and rejects all required-field violations.
- Deterministic serialization produces identical bytes for identical logical content.
- Template examples committed under `docs/reproducibility/`.
- At least 20 unit tests covering normal, boundary, and adversarial cases.

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by**: None (foundational governance bead).
- **Blocks**: bd-2ql (benchmark suite needs repro contracts), bd-2n9 (denominator calculator publishes results with contracts), bd-1nn (flamegraph pipeline stores results with contracts), all downstream benchmark/claim publishing beads.
- **Parent**: bd-2mf (10.1 Charter + Governance epic).

title: [10.1] Add donor-extraction scope document with explicit exclusions for V8/QuickJS semantic harvesting
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.1 (Charter + Governance), item 4. Cross-refs: 4.1 (Execution Strategy Decision: Spec-First Hybrid Bootstrap), 4 (Non-Negotiable Constraints), 8.8 (Verified Self-Replacement Architecture).

## What
Produce a formal donor-extraction scope document that explicitly defines what may and may not be extracted from V8 and QuickJS source code for use as semantic reference material. This document is the legal and technical boundary between "donor consultation" and "implementation source of truth," ensuring FrankenEngine builds from extracted specifications rather than architectural blueprints or line-by-line translations.

## Detailed Requirements
1. **Inclusion scope**: Observable behavior specifications (input/output contracts, error semantics, edge-case behavior for ES2020 normative operations), conformance test vectors (test262 mappings), and semantic reference points for parser/IR/execution decisions.
2. **Exclusion scope (explicit)**: Internal V8/QuickJS architecture patterns (hidden class systems, inline caches, specific GC algorithms, JIT compiler design, internal object representation layouts), optimization strategies that are V8/QuickJS-specific rather than spec-derived, and any code that could create licensing entanglement.
3. **Boundary rules**: 
   - Donor code may be READ for understanding observable semantics; it may NOT be TRANSLATED line-by-line into Rust.
   - Extracted semantics must be documented as standalone specification artifacts (natural language + formal invariants) before any implementation begins.
   - Implementation phases consume only the approved spec artifacts, never raw donor source.
4. **Governance**: 
   - Every extraction must be logged with donor file path, extracted semantic description, and extraction date.
   - A review checklist must confirm each extraction is behavioral (not architectural).
   - The document must be signed off before any donor-informed implementation begins.
5. **Format**: Markdown document committed at `docs/governance/donor_extraction_scope.md` with structured sections for each exclusion category.

## Rationale

title: [DUPLICATE of bd-2u0] Reproducibility contract - IGNORE
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.1, item 3. Cross-refs: 7.5 (Fairness + Reproducibility Rules), 14.3 (Reproducibility + Neutral Verification), 11 (Evidence And Decision Contracts).

## Background
FrankenEngine makes significant performance and security claims (>=3x throughput, >=10x compromise reduction, <=250ms containment). These claims are only credible if third parties can independently reproduce them. The plan mandates (Section 7.5) that all runs use identical hardware/OS envelopes, published full CLI/env manifests, fixed dataset seeds, and deterministic repro commands. Section 14.3 requires one-command neutral verifier mode.

## What
Define and implement a reproducibility contract template consisting of three canonical artifacts:
1. **env.json**: Hardware/OS envelope (CPU model, cores, RAM, kernel version, OS version, compiler version, runtime flags, linked library versions). Must be machine-parseable and diff-friendly.
2. **manifest.json**: Run manifest capturing runtime versions (Node LTS pin, Bun stable pin, FrankenEngine commit), dataset checksums, seed transcripts, harness commit IDs, configuration flags, and policy artifact hashes.
3. **repro.lock**: Lockfile binding env+manifest to specific reproducible run state. Includes content hashes for all input artifacts, expected output checksums, and a deterministic repro command that can be copy-pasted for reruns.

## Rationale/Justification
Without a standardized reproducibility contract, benchmark claims become fragile narratives rather than verifiable facts. The plan explicitly requires (Section 14.3): 'Require at least two independent third-party reruns before category-level claims are treated as externally validated.' This is impossible without machine-readable reproducibility contracts. This template also supports the evidence-and-decision-contracts requirement (Section 11) that every major proposal includes benchmark and correctness artifacts.

## Detailed Requirements
- Template files must be versioned with schema_version field for forward compatibility
- env.json must auto-detect current environment via a CLI command (e.g., franken-engine env snapshot)
- manifest.json must include content hashes (SHA-256) for all input artifacts referenced
- repro.lock must include a single deterministic command line that reproduces the run
- All three files must use deterministic JSON serialization (sorted keys, no trailing commas) for diff-friendliness
- Templates must be extensible: additional fields can be added without breaking existing parsers
- Integration point: benchmark harness (10.6, bd-2ql) must emit these files automatically on every run
- Integration point: frankensqlite-backed result ledgers (Section 7.5) must store and index these artifacts
- Integration point: neutral verifier mode (Section 14.3) must consume these files as input

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: schema validation, auto-detection of env fields, deterministic serialization round-trip
- Integration test: run a benchmark, verify env.json/manifest.json/repro.lock are emitted, re-run using repro.lock and verify identical outputs
- E2E test: cross-machine reproducibility — verify that repro.lock from machine A produces same results on machine B (modulo documented env constraints)
- Golden vector tests: known env/manifest/repro.lock files parse correctly across versions

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Template files defined with versioned schemas and documentation
2. CLI command for auto-generating env.json from current environment
3. Benchmark harness integration point defined and documented
4. Schema validation passes for all template files
5. Cross-version compatibility tested (old schema files still parse with new reader)
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-2u0 (reproducibility contract) as stated in title

title: [DUPLICATE of bd-10a] Donor-extraction scope - IGNORE
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.1, item 4. Cross-refs: 4.1 (Execution Strategy Decision: Spec-First Hybrid Bootstrap), 4 (Non-Negotiable Constraints), 8.7 (Multi-Level IR Design Contract).

## Background
FrankenEngine's execution strategy (Section 4.1) is 'Spec-First Hybrid Bootstrap': use V8/QuickJS only as semantic donor corpora, NOT as architectural blueprints. The plan states: 'Use donor engines to extract behavior specifications and conformance vectors, not architectural blueprints. Implement from extracted specifications in native Rust crates; never line-by-line translate donor code.' This document is the first deliverable in the execution strategy decision contract.

## What
Produce a formal donor-extraction scope document that defines:
1. **In-scope extractions**: Which observable behaviors, edge cases, and conformance vectors are being harvested from V8 and QuickJS. This includes ES2020 normative semantics, Promise/microtask ordering, closure/scope behavior, prototype chain semantics, property descriptor behavior, iterator/generator protocols, and module resolution rules.
2. **Explicit exclusions**: What is intentionally NOT ported or mirrored. This includes: V8 hidden classes/inline caches architecture, V8 Turbofan/Ignition pipeline design, QuickJS bytecode format, V8/QuickJS GC algorithms, V8/QuickJS internal object layouts, any engine-specific optimization heuristics.
3. **Extraction methodology**: How semantic information is extracted (test262 conformance, differential testing, specification reading, behavioral observation) vs what constitutes prohibited architectural copying.
4. **Legal/IP boundary**: Clear statement that only observable behavioral specifications are used, not copyrighted internal implementations.

## Rationale/Justification
Section 4 (Non-Negotiable Constraints) explicitly forbids runtime wrappers/bindings around upstream engines and states legacy_quickjs/ and legacy_v8/ are 'reference corpora for ideas and test vectors only.' Without a formal scope document, there is risk of inadvertent architectural mirroring, which would undermine the de novo design thesis and create technical/legal liability. The document also serves as a reference for all downstream implementation beads to verify they are working from extracted specs, not donor code.

## Detailed Requirements
- Document must enumerate every behavior domain being extracted (e.g., 'ES2020 §12.3 Property Accessors: observable get/set behavior and ordering semantics')
- Document must enumerate explicit exclusions with justification (e.g., 'V8 hidden classes: excluded because FrankenEngine uses its own object model optimized for capability tracking')
- Document must define extraction methodology: behavioral observation via test cases, not code reading
- Document must define the boundary between 'learning from donor behavior' (OK) and 'copying donor architecture' (NOT OK)
- Document must be version-controlled and updated when new extraction domains are added
- Cross-reference: the semantic donor spec document (bd-3u5) consumes this scope document as its input contract

## Testing Requirements
- Review gate: document reviewed by project owner before downstream implementation begins
- Compliance check: random audit of implementation code against exclusion list to verify no architectural mirroring
- Traceability: each implementation bead in 10.2 (VM Core) should be traceable to an extraction in this document or to a FrankenEngine-original design decision

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Scope document produced with enumerated in-scope extractions and explicit exclusions
2. Extraction methodology section clearly distinguishes behavioral observation from architectural copying
3. Legal/IP boundary statement included
4. Cross-reference to bd-3u5 (semantic donor spec) established
5. Document version-controlled in the repository

title: [review][product_blocker_ledger] Validate readiness statuses against support-surface vocabulary
description: Review finding from commit e4e60e8d (feat(product_blocker_ledger): fail-closed on contradictory support-contract statuses [RGC-408B]). The new contradiction check in crates/franken-engine/src/bin/franken_engine_product_blocker_ledger.rs:370-424 only deserializes readiness_answer_contract and compares the ready/blocked arrays to each other. It does not parse the top-level allowed_support_statuses or surface_rows from docs/support_surface_contract.json, so a caller using RGC_ENGINE_PRODUCT_BLOCKER_LEDGER_SUPPORT_CONTRACT_PATH can provide an otherwise well-formed contract where engine_ready_when_support_status_in or engine_blocked_when_support_status_in contains an unknown status such as 'ga_ready' or 'not_real'. validate_support_contract still passes as long as 'shipped' and one blocked entry exist and the unknown value is not contradictory. Downstream handoff/report scripts treat readiness arrays as the machine-readable answer key for surface_rows[].support_status, so accepting unknown readiness values weakens the fail-closed support-surface contract and can make product-readiness artifacts classify rows under vocabulary the canonical support-surface tests would reject. Fix by deserializing allowed_support_statuses and surface_rows in the blocker-ledger input contract, requiring every readiness status to be nonblank, allowed, and preferably represented by at least one surface row (or explicitly documented as reserved), and add emit_bundle regressions for unknown ready and blocked statuses.

title: [10.8] Add runtime diagnostics and evidence export CLI.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.8, item 1. Cross-refs: 9E.9 (normative observability surface), 10.11 (evidence-ledger schema), 10.13 (control-plane invariants dashboard).

## What
Add runtime diagnostics and evidence export CLI. Operators need a single command to inspect runtime state, export evidence for incident investigation, and verify system health.

## Detailed Requirements
- Diagnostics CLI: show current runtime state (loaded extensions, active policies, security epoch, GC pressure, scheduler lane utilization)
- Evidence export: export evidence ledger entries for a time range, extension, or incident trace_id
- Format: structured JSON output for machine consumption, human-readable summary mode
- Export must include: decision receipts, hostcall telemetry, containment actions, policy changes, replay artifacts
- Filter support: by extension_id, trace_id, time range, severity, decision type
- Deterministic export: same query on same data produces identical output (for audit)

## Rationale
The plan requires operational readiness (Phase E) with evidence-backed operational reports. Operators cannot manage a system they cannot inspect. The evidence export CLI is the primary interface for post-incident forensics (9A.3) and audit compliance. Without it, the deterministic evidence graph has no practical access point.

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: diagnostics command returns structured runtime state
- Unit tests: evidence export produces valid JSON with expected schema
- Unit tests: filters correctly narrow results (by extension, trace_id, time range)
- Integration test: export evidence for a simulated incident, verify completeness
- Determinism test: same query → same output across runs

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: evidence ledger (10.11), hostcall telemetry (10.5), containment actions (10.5)
- Blocks: Phase E exit gate (operational readiness report), operator workflows

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid/adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end/integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds/fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (`trace_id`, `decision_id`, `policy_id`, `component`, `event`, `outcome`, `error_code`) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build/test workflows introduced by this bead, document/execute via `rch`-wrapped commands for heavy compilation/test workloads.

title: [RGC-920] Close the remaining placeholder/mock/stub debt surfaced by the zero-placeholder audit
description:
This epic turns the repo-wide placeholder/mock/stub audit into an implementation-ordered remediation graph. The audit found no live production `todo!()`/`unimplemented!()` in workspace crates, but it did find eight remaining debt surfaces that still behave like placeholders, mocks, stale truth surfaces, or explicit stubs:

1. Live shipped JSON compound placeholder semantics in `crates/franken-engine/src/stdlib.rs`: `json_parse` returns `[json-compound:<len>]` for arrays/objects and `json_stringify` returns `[json-object]` for objects/functions.
2. Dead exported stub symbol in `crates/franken-extension-host/src/lib.rs`: `placeholder_extension_host_symbol()`.
3. Architectural mock exposure in `crates/franken-engine/src/control_plane/mod.rs` because `pub mod mocks` is reachable from the production surface.
4. Internally contradictory lowering truth surface in `crates/franken-engine/src/lowering_gap_inventory.rs`: every site is described as `Resolved` while `execution_ready_semantics` is hard-coded `false` for every site.
5. Stale control-plane mock inventory in `crates/franken-engine/src/control_plane_mock_inventory.rs`: it still records production mock occurrences that direct source search no longer shows, while also correctly flagging the still-real ungated mock module.
6. Literal placeholder flamegraph generation in `scripts/generate_parser_phase0_artifacts.sh`.
7. Placeholder artifact backfill in `scripts/run_parser_oracle_gate.sh::write_placeholders()`.
8. Missing final closure proof that the existing zero-placeholder gate and waiver discipline cover all of the above.

This workstream should proceed in a strict order: remove live shipped runtime placeholders first; remove or quarantine dead/mock public surfaces second; reconcile stale inventories and artifact contracts third; then run repo-wide closure verification and explicit waiver checks last.
design:
Treat the findings as three different problem classes, not one cleanup bucket.

1. Shipped semantic placeholders. These are product behavior defects and must be replaced with real semantics, not hidden behind richer placeholder strings.
2. Stub or mock surface leakage. These are architecture and API-boundary defects. The fix is to remove the dead stub or make the test-only surface un-importable from production code by default.
3. Stale or placeholder truth surfaces. Inventories, manifests, and operator artifacts must become source-derived or fail-closed so they cannot silently drift into fiction.

Cross-cutting rules for the subtree:
- Do not create new “temporary compatibility” placeholders. Any intentionally unsupported behavior must fail closed or surface as an explicit bounded contract.
- Prefer source-derived inventory generation and freshness guards over manual ledgers that can drift.
- Final closure must run through the existing zero-placeholder scan/gate/waiver infrastructure instead of inventing a second, parallel sign-off path.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every audit finding mapped in this bead is either fixed or converted into an explicit, bounded, owner-routed unsupported contract with deterministic artifacts.
2. Each child contract or implementation bead ships focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid/adversarial inputs, and regression cases appropriate to its surface.
3. Each child implementation or verification bead ships deterministic scenario/e2e/replay scripts that emit `run_manifest.json`, `events.jsonl`, `commands.txt`, `trace_ids.json`, `step_logs/`, and bead-specific report artifacts.
4. Structured logs across the subtree assert stable fields including `trace_id`, `component`, `event`, `outcome`, `error_code`, and domain-specific identifiers needed for replay and operator triage.
5. No shipped runtime path still returns placeholder descriptors for compound JSON semantics, and no production-default crate surface exposes the dead extension-host stub or the control-plane mock helpers.
6. Lowering/mock inventories and parser artifact scripts emit truthful, source-derived, or fail-closed outputs rather than stale or anonymous placeholder data.
7. A deterministic closure bundle proves the state of every mapped finding through tests, scanners, and operator-grade artifacts, with any residual waiver state made explicit.
8. Any CPU-intensive Rust build/test/clippy/e2e workflow under this subtree is executed via `rch`.
notes:
Upstream context:
- `bd-1lsy.9.5.1` built the scanner and subsystem inventories that surfaced this debt.
- `bd-1lsy.9.5.2` is the existing enforcement bead for zero-placeholder semantics and explicit waivers.

Execution guidance:
- Claim leaf beads first; do not claim this umbrella directly while child leaves remain open.
- The intent is that future agents can work from this bead tree alone without reopening the original audit writeup.

title: [RGC-920A] Replace live JSON compound placeholders with real runtime semantics
description: Replace the remaining live JSON compound placeholders in `crates/franken-engine/src/stdlib.rs`. Today `json_parse` only materializes scalars and returns a descriptor string for arrays/objects, while `json_stringify` returns `[json-object]` for object/function cases. Those are shipped semantics, not just diagnostics, so this bead owns the real runtime contract for compound JSON values and the proof that placeholder descriptors are gone from the shipped path.
design:
Handle the JSON work as a single semantic slice with four internal steps.

1. Define the supported compound JSON contract across parse and stringify: runtime ownership model, array/object representation, deterministic property ordering expectations, unsupported edge behavior, and exact error model.
2. Replace descriptor-returning parse behavior with real heap-backed array/object materialization, including nested compound values.
3. Replace object/function stringify placeholders with real traversal logic, explicit omission/rejection rules, and deterministic failure for unsupported cases such as cycles if they are not yet supported.
4. Prove closure with unit tests, shipped-path parity scenarios, and scanner expectations so the zero-placeholder gate can treat this area as genuinely remediated.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `JSON.parse` no longer returns synthetic descriptor strings for arrays/objects in the shipped stdlib surface.
2. `JSON.stringify` no longer returns `[json-object]` for runtime object/array cases; the output is derived from real traversal semantics.
3. The supported compound JSON contract covers representation, ordering, explicit unsupported edges, and deterministic failure behavior instead of placeholder collapse.

title: [RGC-920C] Seal control-plane mock helpers behind an explicit test-only surface
description: Seal the control-plane mock helpers behind an explicit test-only surface. Even though the live runtime no longer appears to depend on `MockCx`/`MockBudget`, `crates/franken-engine/src/control_plane/mod.rs` still exports `pub mod mocks`, which means production-default code can reach test scaffolding. This bead removes that architectural leak without stranding the current test suites that rely on the helpers.
design: Choose a deliberate exposure strategy first: `#[cfg(test)]`, a test-support feature gate, or a separate test-only module/crate. Then migrate all current unit/integration consumers onto that path and tighten the ambient mock guard so the production surface fails closed if a future change reopens direct mock access. The objective is not merely “no runtime call sites today”; it is “production-default code cannot import test scaffolding by accident tomorrow.”
acceptance_criteria:
1. The production-default crate surface no longer exposes the control-plane mock helpers directly, while test suites retain an explicit supported path to the scaffolding they need.
2. Comprehensive unit/integration tests cover production-default builds, explicit test-enabled builds, import-path regressions, and policy violations.
3. Deterministic scenario/e2e scripts emit `run_manifest.json`, `events.jsonl`, `commands.txt`, `trace_ids.json`, `step_logs/`, `control_plane_mock_surface_report.json`, and `control_plane_mock_guard_report.json`.
4. Structured logs, ambient-mock diagnostics, and inventory outputs fail closed on future production mock exposure; heavy Rust verification runs via `rch`.
notes: Aligned the control_plane_integration regression with the actual working-tree architecture: control-plane mock helpers are removed from crates/franken-engine/src/control_plane/mod.rs and consumed from frankenengine-test-support, so the regression now asserts absence of  rather than a gated runtime export.

title: [RGC-920C.3] Harden ambient mock guard and inventory expectations against future production exposure
description: Lock the boundary down after the refactor. This leaf updates ambient mock guard logic, inventory expectations, and regression tests so any future production mock exposure is caught immediately.
design: Treat the guard and inventory as the policy backstop for the new architecture. The post-refactor source tree should become the new baseline, and regressions should fail closed.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Guard and inventory expectations are updated to the post-refactor architecture.
2. Regression tests inject or simulate future production mock exposure and prove it is flagged as a failure with actionable diagnostics.
3. Deterministic scenario/replay scripts emit `run_manifest.json`, `events.jsonl`, `commands.txt`, `trace_ids.json`, `step_logs/`, and `control_plane_mock_guard_regression_report.json`.
4. Structured logs include stable fields `trace_id`, `component`, `event`, `outcome`, `error_code`, plus rule IDs, diagnostic codes, and source-path metadata for replay and triage.
5. Any CPU-intensive Rust verification runs via `rch`.

title: [RGC-920D] Reconcile lowering-gap inventory truth with actual execution readiness
description: Reconcile the lowering-gap inventory with reality. `crates/franken-engine/src/lowering_gap_inventory.rs` currently labels every tracked site as `Resolved` and uses resolved prose in multiple fields, but `LoweringGapSiteDescriptor::from_site` still hard-codes `execution_ready_semantics: false` for every site. That makes the inventory internally contradictory and contaminates downstream consumers such as the zero-placeholder scan and any operator who trusts the emitted manifest counts.
design: Start by defining the invariant between `status`, `execution_consequence`, `user_visible_divergence`, and `execution_ready_semantics`. Then either derive the readiness flags from truthful current semantics or downgrade the status/prose to match reality. The end state must be internally consistent and machine-checkable: the inventory, run manifest, events, and downstream scanners should all tell the same story without relying on human reinterpretation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No lowering-gap site descriptor presents a resolved narrative while simultaneously encoding contradictory readiness state without explanation.
2. Inventory counts, run-manifest counts, event details, and downstream consumer views agree on one truthful readiness model.
3. Focused unit/regression tests cover invariant enforcement, generator behavior, consumer parity, and regression against contradictory truth surfaces.
4. Deterministic scenario/replay scripts emit `run_manifest.json`, `events.jsonl`, `commands.txt`, `trace_ids.json`, `step_logs/`, and `lowering_gap_truth_reconciliation_report.json`.
5. Structured logs make site-level before/after truth-state transitions and failure causes explicit; heavy Rust verification runs via `rch`.
notes:
Audit evidence:
- `crates/franken-engine/src/lowering_gap_inventory.rs:115-123`
- `crates/franken-engine/src/lowering_gap_inventory.rs:278-296`

title: [10.9] Release gate: PLAS is active for prioritized extension cohorts with signed `capability_witness` artifacts and escrow-path replay evidence (implementation ownership: `10.15`).
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.9, item 6 -- Moonshot Disruption Track (release gates for frontier programs).

## What
This is a **release gate**, not an implementation task. It verifies that the Permission-Less Authority System (PLAS) -- built by the Delta Moonshots track (10.15) -- is active for the prioritized extension cohorts, with every authority grant backed by a signed `capability_witness` artifact and escrow-path replay evidence. The gate confirms that PLAS is not merely deployed but is operating with full cryptographic accountability for authority decisions.

The gate owner does not build PLAS; the gate owner validates that the deployed PLAS meets the signed-witness and escrow-path completeness bar for the designated extension cohorts.

## Gate Criteria
1. PLAS is active (not in shadow/audit-only mode) for all extensions in the prioritized cohort list.
2. Every capability grant produces a signed `capability_witness` artifact containing: grantee identity, capability set, grant timestamp, policy version, and grantor signature.
3. `capability_witness` signatures are verifiable using the published trust anchor (public key / certificate chain) without requiring access to the granting service.
4. Escrow-path replay evidence exists for every grant: a deterministic replay from the escrow log reproduces the same grant decision given the same policy version and request context.
5. Revocation of a granted capability produces a corresponding signed revocation witness, and the escrow log reflects the revocation event.
6. No extension in the prioritized cohort operates with ambient authority -- every permission is traceable to a `capability_witness`.

## Implementation Ownership
- **10.15 (Delta Moonshots):** Builds PLAS runtime, `capability_witness` signing infrastructure, escrow-path logging, and revocation flow. Encompasses 9I moonshots: PLAS, TEE-Bound Receipts, Verified Self-Replacement.
- **10.9 (this gate):** Validates witness completeness, signature verifiability, escrow-path replayability, and cohort coverage.

## Rationale
PLAS is a category-defining capability that eliminates ambient authority for extensions -- a property no mainstream JS/TS runtime offers. However, the capability is only meaningful if every authority decision is cryptographically witnessed and replayable. A PLAS deployment where some grants lack witnesses or where escrow replay fails is worse than no PLAS at all, because it creates a false sense of security. This gate ensures the deployed system meets the full accountability bar, feeding the `autonomy_delta` dimension of the disruption scorecard (bd-6pk).

Related 9I moonshots: PLAS, TEE-Bound Receipts, Verified Self-Replacement.
Related 9F moonshots: Capability-Typed TS, Cryptographic Receipts.

## Verification Requirements
- **Cohort coverage audit:** Enumerate all extensions in the prioritized cohort; confirm each has PLAS active (not shadow mode) with at least one exercised `capability_witness`.
- **Witness signature verification:** For a sample of grants, independently verify `capability_witness` signatures using only the published trust anchor and the artifact bundle.
- **Escrow replay:** For a sample of grants, replay the escrow log from a clean state and confirm the replayed decision matches the original grant.
- **Revocation round-trip:** Grant a capability, revoke it, and confirm both the grant witness and revocation witness are present in the escrow log with correct signatures.
- **Ambient authority scan:** Run a static/dynamic analysis pass confirming no extension in the cohort holds permissions not traceable to a `capability_witness`.
- **Scorecard integration:** Results feed `autonomy_delta` in the disruption scorecard (bd-6pk).
- **Structured logging:** PLAS operations emit structured logs with fields: `trace_id`, `extension_id`, `capability_set`, `witness_hash`, `grant_or_revoke`, `policy_version`, `escrow_sequence`, `signature_valid`.

## Dependencies
- bd-6pk (disruption scorecard) -- gate results feed `autonomy_delta` dimension.
- bd-181 (GA native lanes gate) -- PLAS coverage is a prerequisite for full native lane operation.
- bd-dkh (proof-specialized lanes gate) -- proof lanes require PLAS-granted capabilities for specialization.
- 10.15 Delta Moonshots track -- delivers the PLAS implementation.
- bd-1xm (parent epic) -- this bead is a child of the Moonshot Disruption Track epic.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.

## Detailed Requirements (Plan-Space Refinement)
- This bead is a release gate and may only close when every declared dependency gate/input is closed with signed and reproducible artifacts.
- Produce a deterministic gate-check runbook (CLI commands, expected outputs, failure codes) that can be executed by an independent operator.
- Attach threshold tables for pass/fail metrics (security, performance, determinism, replay, operational safety) and document rationale for each threshold.
- Include explicit rollback/fallback activation criteria and validated recovery commands for gate failure scenarios.
- Require gate-specific end-to-end validation scripts and structured log assertions proving the gate result is reproducible and auditable.

title: [10.11] Implement O(Delta) anti-entropy reconciliation for distributed revocation/checkpoint/evidence object sets.
description:
## Plan Reference
- **Section**: 10.11 item 30 (FrankenSQLite-Inspired Runtime Systems Track)
- **9G Cross-ref**: 9G.10 — O(Delta) anti-entropy + proof-carrying recovery
- **Top-10 Links**: #5 (Supply-chain trust fabric), #10 (Provenance + revocation fabric)

## What
Implement O(Delta) anti-entropy reconciliation for distributed revocation, checkpoint, and evidence object sets. Instead of full-state synchronization, nodes exchange compact set-difference summaries (IBLT-style) to efficiently identify and resolve discrepancies proportional to the actual difference.

## Detailed Requirements
1. Implement an IBLT (Invertible Bloom Lookup Table) based set-reconciliation protocol:
   - Each node maintains an IBLT encoding of its current object set (revocation events, checkpoint markers, evidence entries).
   - Reconciliation: two nodes exchange IBLTs, compute the symmetric difference, and each node retrieves the missing objects.
   - Communication cost: O(|Delta|) where Delta is the number of differing objects, not O(|total set|).
2. Object types for reconciliation:
   - \`RevocationEvent\`: revocation issuance and propagation records.
   - \`CheckpointMarker\`: policy checkpoint and decision markers from the marker stream (bd-3e7).
   - \`EvidenceEntry\`: evidence-ledger entries (bd-33h).
3. Reconciliation protocol:
   - Step 1: Nodes exchange IBLT sketches (compact, fixed-size regardless of set size).
   - Step 2: Compute set difference (subtract IBLTs).
   - Step 3: Decode difference to identify missing/extra objects on each side.
   - Step 4: Request and transfer missing objects.
   - Step 5: Verify received objects (content hash, epoch validity, chain consistency via MMR proofs from bd-2h2).
   - Step 6: Emit reconciliation evidence: \`reconciliation_id\`, \`peer\`, \`objects_sent\`, \`objects_received\`, \`objects_conflicting\`, \`duration_ms\`, \`epoch_id\`, \`trace_id\`.
4. Failure handling: if the IBLT cannot successfully peel (decode the difference), the protocol falls back to the deterministic fallback protocol (bd-117).
5. Epoch scoping: reconciliation is scoped to objects within the current epoch or a configured lookback window. Old-epoch objects are handled by the fallback protocol.
6. Concurrency: reconciliation operations use the \`RemoteInFlight\` bulkhead (bd-289) and idempotency keys (bd-359) for retry safety.
7. Convergence SLO: under normal operation, reconciliation must converge within a configurable bound (default: 30 seconds for < 1000 differences).

## Rationale
Full-state synchronization is O(n) and impractical at scale. The 9G.10 contract requires O(Delta) reconciliation so that trust-critical state (revocations, checkpoints, evidence) converges efficiently across fleet nodes. IBLT-based reconciliation is well-studied and provides the necessary efficiency. Combined with MMR consistency proofs (bd-2h2) and proof-carrying recovery (bd-2j3), this creates a distributed trust fabric that is both efficient and verifiable — directly supporting Section 3.2 item 9.

## Testing Requirements
- **Unit tests**: Verify IBLT encoding and decoding for known sets. Verify set-difference computation. Verify peel success for small differences. Verify peel failure detection for large differences.
- **Property tests**: Generate random set pairs with known differences; verify reconciliation correctly identifies all differences. Vary difference sizes and verify O(Delta) communication cost.
- **Integration tests**: Run two nodes with divergent object sets, execute reconciliation, and verify convergence. Verify evidence emission. Verify bulkhead and idempotency usage.
- **Failure tests**: Simulate IBLT peel failure and verify fallback to deterministic protocol (bd-117).
- **Convergence tests**: Measure reconciliation time for various difference sizes and verify it meets the convergence SLO.
- **Logging/observability**: Reconciliation events carry full structured fields for monitoring and debugging.

## Implementation Notes
- IBLT implementation: use a standard IBLT with configurable bucket count (rule of thumb: 1.5x expected difference size).
- Object identity: use Tier 2 ContentHash (bd-4hf) for IBLT keys.
- Consider a multi-round protocol for robustness: if first IBLT exchange fails to peel, increase bucket count and retry before falling back.
- Network transport: use named computations (bd-3s3) for reconciliation messages.
- Persistence: IBLT state can be reconstructed from the persisted object sets; no need to persist the IBLT itself.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: bd-4hf (hash strategy for object identity), bd-3e7 (marker stream for checkpoint objects), bd-33h (evidence entries as reconciled objects), bd-2h2 (MMR proofs for consistency verification), bd-hli (remote capability gate), bd-289 (remote in-flight bulkhead), bd-359 (idempotency keys), bd-3s3 (named computations for messages).
- Blocks: bd-117 (deterministic fallback when reconciliation fails), bd-2j3 (proof-carrying recovery for reconciliation outcomes).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Implement the full objective with deterministic behavior, explicit failure semantics, and safe fallback/rollback rules.
- Add focused unit tests for normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
- Add integration and/or end-to-end test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions, degraded mode, and recovery behavior with deterministic fixtures.
- Emit structured logs with stable keys (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and assert critical events in tests.
- Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, evidence pointers, replay pointers, benchmark/check outputs) plus clear operator verification steps.
- Ensure heavy Rust build/test execution paths are documented and run through rch wrappers when implementation begins.

title: [10.6] Implement benchmark denominator calculator (`weighted geometric mean`) and publication gate for Node/Bun comparisons.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.6, item 2. Cross-refs: Section 14.2 (>= 3x Claim Denominator Normative), Phase C exit gate.

## What
Implement the benchmark denominator calculator using weighted geometric mean, with publication gates that enforce the >= 3x claim validity rules from Section 14.2.

## Detailed Requirements
- Per-case speedup: r_i = throughput_franken_engine_i / throughput_B_i for each baseline B in {Node, Bun}
- Suite score: S_B = exp(sum_i w_i * ln(r_i)) with non-zero weights summing to 1
- Default weighting: equal weighting across family/profile cells
- Publication gate for >= 3x claim: S_Node >= 3.0 AND S_Bun >= 3.0 AND all cases pass behavior-equivalence
- Failed-equivalence invalidation: any failed behavior-equivalence case invalidates claim publication until fixed or excluded via versioned benchmark-spec revision
- Throughput claims must be accompanied by latency/error envelopes (speedups cannot hide tail-collapse)
- Publication includes: native-coverage progression and per-slot replacement lineage IDs (Section 14.3)

## Rationale
The >= 3x claim is a hard, normative requirement (Section 14.2). The weighted geometric mean prevents cherry-picking: a single fast case cannot compensate for many slow cases. The behavior-equivalence gate prevents inflating throughput by dropping work or relaxing correctness. This calculator is the mathematical foundation of the project's primary performance claim.

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: weighted geometric mean calculation on known inputs produces expected output
- Unit tests: publication gate passes when S >= 3.0 for both baselines
- Unit tests: publication gate fails when any case fails equivalence
- Unit tests: publication gate fails when S < 3.0 for either baseline
- Edge cases: single case (trivial), all equal speedups, one extreme outlier
- Verify weight normalization (sum to 1)

## Implementation Notes
- Implement as library function for programmatic use + CLI for CI integration
- Use f64 arithmetic with explicit rounding rules for reproducibility
- Consider storing calculation artifacts in frankensqlite for audit trail
- Publication report should be machine-readable (JSON) for CI gates

## Dependencies

- Blocks: Phase C exit gate, Section 14.2 claim publication

title: [HIGH] [REVIEW] Test262 golden generator emits mock V8/QuickJS fixtures
description:
Reality-check scope: AGENTS.md/RUNTIME_CHARTER donor-corpus rule versus Test262 golden fixture generation.

Docs claim: AGENTS.md:134-135 and docs/RUNTIME_CHARTER.md:14-21 forbid binding-led core execution and allow legacy_v8/ and legacy_quickjs/ only as reference corpora for semantics/tests. That boundary is mostly honored: Cargo has no rusty_v8/rquickjs/QuickJS/V8 engine dependency, no Rust source imports legacy_quickjs or legacy_v8, and QuickJs/V8 execution lanes instantiate the native InterpreterCore.

Reality gap: crates/franken-engine/src/test262_conformance_runner.rs:1280-1308 exposes generate_golden_fixtures(), whose comment says it should check for d8/qjs binaries in legacy_v8/legacy_quickjs, execute each test, and store golden outputs. The implementation instead creates mock ExpectedOutput values with stdout strings like "V8 output for <test>" and "QuickJS output for <test>" and available=false. This means a source-level golden generator can appear to refresh donor-reference fixtures without actually using the reference corpus or real reference engines.

Impact: not a core execution binding violation, but it is a proof/evidence truth gap. Any workflow that relies on generate_golden_fixtures() as donor-reference evidence could produce synthetic V8/QuickJS fixture text rather than observed reference-engine outputs, undermining compatibility/conformance claims.

Reproducer/audit commands:
```bash
rg -n "Mock golden fixture generation|V8 output for|QuickJS output for|generate_golden_fixtures" crates/franken-engine/src/test262_conformance_runner.rs
rg -n "rusty_v8|rquickjs|legacy_(quickjs|v8)::|include_str!.*legacy_(quickjs|v8)" Cargo.toml Cargo.lock crates/franken-engine/src
```

Acceptance: either remove/disable generate_golden_fixtures() until it can call real reference-engine tooling, or implement it so fixture outputs are produced from explicit d8/qjs/reference-engine commands with command ledger, exit codes, hashes, and unavailable-state handling. Synthetic placeholders must not be emitted as golden reference data.

title: [HIGH][REVIEW] sqlmodel_rust boundary is not enforced for typed-heavy persistence stores
description:
AGENTS.md says to use /dp/sqlmodel_rust when typed model/schema layers are beneficial. ADR-0004 and docs/FRANKENSQLITE_PERSISTENCE_INVENTORY.md identify replacement lineage log, IFC provenance index, and specialization index as usually requiring sqlmodel_rust over frankensqlite.

Evidence:
- docs/FRANKENSQLITE_PERSISTENCE_INVENTORY.md marks replacement lineage log, IFC provenance index, and specialization index as 'sqlmodel_rust on frankensqlite'.
- crates/franken-engine/src/storage_adapter.rs collapses every StoreKind, including ReplacementLineage, IfcProvenance, and SpecializationIndex, into generic StoreRecord/StoreQuery/BatchPutEntry records.
- There is no sqlmodel_rust dependency, no /dp/sqlmodel_rust path integration, and no guard that fails when a typed-heavy store is implemented through raw StoreRecord shapes.

Why this matters: the repo has documentation asserting the typed-model decision, but implementation and tests can drift into raw generic persistence for stores whose invariants are supposed to be enforced at typed boundaries.

Expected fix: bind typed-heavy stores to concrete /dp/sqlmodel_rust model/schema APIs or add a policy guard that rejects raw StoreRecord-only implementations for inventory rows marked 'sqlmodel_rust on frankensqlite' unless an approved exception exists.

title: [CRITICAL] resource_escalation_control::execute_escalation returns hardcoded fixture data, ignores all inputs
description:
ResourceEscalationController::execute_escalation in crates/franken-engine/src/resource_escalation_control.rs:362+ returns the same canned escalation log on every call regardless of inputs:

- Throttle event hardcodes estimated_wait_ns=150_000_000, position=3, utilization_millionths=880_000 (lines 374-392). The bounded_dimensions parameter never influences the throttle decision.
- Sandbox event hardcodes verdict=MultipleViolations and a fixed certificate snapshot (CPU 112000/100000, heap 75497472/67108864) on lines 396-419, with no derivation from inputs or actual budget state.
- Suspend event always uses LaneAction::SuspendAdaptive on lines 423-435, never consulting decision_context (which is a field but is annotated #[allow(dead_code)] in commit 9f0f9e19 because it is genuinely unread).
- Terminate event hardcodes utilization_millionths=1_250_000, escalation_attempts=3, and final_measurements={CpuTime:125000, HeapMemory:80000000} on lines 440-461.

Symptoms confirming this is fixture code, not an enforcement API:
- Compiler warnings before commit 9f0f9e19: MILLIONTHS constant unused, ResourceEscalationController.epoch and .decision_context fields never read. Now masked with #[allow(dead_code)] rather than wired up.
- The bounded_dimensions input only flows into EscalationLog::bounded_budget_dimensions field; it does not gate any branch.
- current_timestamp_ns input is only added as a baseline to the four fixed offsets (0/150ms/300ms/450ms).

Why this matters:
- The module advertises in its doc comment 'a first-class deterministic API for resource exhaustion escalation that drives the full sequence: throttle -> sandbox -> suspend -> terminate' and emits a content_hash for replay stability. Replay is meaningless when the artifact is identical for every call.
- ESCALATION_BEAD_ID='bd-g61cl' is asserted closed by commit 63cf0167; downstream consumers (GA evidence package, decision artifacts) may rely on this surface for real escalation evidence.

Acceptance criteria:
- execute_escalation must derive the throttle AdmissionDecision from real queueing_admission_control state.
- The sandbox stage must materialise actual GovernanceVerdict + over-budget certificates from resource_certificate_governance for the workload.
- The suspend stage must invoke runtime_decision_theory::DecisionContext to choose the LaneAction (or skip when not warranted).
- The terminate stage must source TerminationReason and final_measurements from observed state, not constants.
- Inputs that cannot drive a real decision (e.g. epoch, decision_context) must either be removed or wired into the corresponding branch; #[allow(dead_code)] is a code smell here, not a fix.
- A regression test must call execute_escalation with two materially different bounded_dimensions and assert the produced EscalationLog differs in at least one of action/basis/utilisation, beyond the bounded_budget_dimensions field.

Discovered during cross-review (Phase 2). Fix in 213dd7bd addressed the content_hash collision separately; this bead captures the larger scaffolding-vs-API gap.

New API satisfies all 6 acceptance criteria from the bead description. (1) execute_escalation_from_inputs takes EscalationInputs.throttle_decision: AdmissionDecision sourced from real queueing_admission_control state. (2) sandbox_verdict: GovernanceVerdict + sandbox_basis blob from resource_certificate_governance. (3) suspend step invokes self.decision_context.decide(&inputs.decision_state) — the LaneAction is derived, not hardcoded. (4) termination_reason and final_measurements come from caller-observed state. (5) Removed #[allow(dead_code)] from epoch and decision_context fields — both now genuinely used (epoch threads policy_epoch into every basis; decision_context.decide() drives the suspend step). (6) Regression test execute_escalation_from_inputs_log_differs_for_materially_different_inputs asserts logs differ in throttle action, terminate action, AND content_hash for materially different inputs. Existing scripted execute_escalation kept (relabeled in doc as a fixture for replay-stability tests/demos) and points production callers at the new method or per-step record_*. title: [10.15] Add shadow-evaluation gate that blocks global model/policy promotion unless privacy-preserving updates improve safety metrics without exceeding privacy budgets.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.15 (Delta Moonshots Execution Track), subsection 9I.2 (Privacy-Preserving Fleet Learning Layer), item 4 of 4.

## What
Add a shadow-evaluation gate that blocks promotion of global model or policy updates unless privacy-preserving updates demonstrably improve safety metrics without exceeding privacy budgets.

## Detailed Requirements
1. Gate evaluation pipeline:
   - Before any aggregated model/policy delta is promoted to production, run it through shadow evaluation against representative replay corpora.
   - Measure safety-metric deltas: false-positive rate, false-negative rate, calibration error, drift-detection accuracy, containment-time improvement.
   - Verify privacy-budget compliance: promotion candidate must not have consumed budget beyond declared epoch limits.
2. Promotion criteria (all must pass):
   - No regression on any safety metric beyond configurable tolerance threshold.
   - Net improvement on at least one safety metric above minimum significance threshold.
   - Privacy budget for the epoch remains within declared limits.
   - Replay determinism: shadow evaluation results must be reproducible from declared artifacts.
3. Gate decision output:
   - Signed `promotion_decision` artifact with: candidate version, evaluation results per metric, budget status, pass/fail verdict, and rollback token.
   - On failure: candidate is rejected with detailed metric-level failure reasons and recommended remediation.
4. Automatic rollback: if a promoted update causes post-deployment metric regression, trigger automatic rollback to previous signed snapshot with incident receipt.
5. Human override path: governance-approved override possible but requires signed justification artifact.

## Rationale
From 9I.2: "Quality gates require: no budget violation, no regression on safety metrics, and no policy-promotion without shadow validation against representative replay corpora." The shadow-evaluation gate is the critical enforcement point that prevents stochastic learning from degrading deterministic decision quality. It converts fleet learning from a trust-me process into a prove-it process.

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: metric computation, threshold comparisons, budget compliance checks, promotion decision artifact generation.
- Integration tests: full promotion pipeline with mock candidate updates, verify gate blocks regressions, verify gate passes improvements, verify rollback on post-deployment regression.
- Property tests: no candidate that violates any criterion can pass the gate regardless of other metric values.
- Replay tests: shadow evaluation produces identical verdicts given identical candidate and replay corpus.

## Implementation Notes
- Replay corpora should be versioned and pinned to specific evaluation epochs for reproducibility.
- Metric computation should use the same statistical framework as the sentinel/guardplane (10.5, 10.11).
- Gate decisions should feed the moonshot portfolio governor (9I.3) for portfolio-level learning-effectiveness tracking.

## Dependencies
- bd-2lt9 (privacy-learning contract for budget semantics).
- bd-3jz8 (budget accountant for budget compliance verification).
- bd-29a1 (randomness transcript for replay determinism of stochastic phases).
- 10.5 (sentinel/guardplane metrics infrastructure).
- 10.7 (conformance and verification infrastructure for shadow evaluation).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.

5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.
