title: [10.15] Add frankensqlite-backed witness/index stores and conformance tests for deterministic witness retrieval and replay joins.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.15 (Delta Moonshots Execution Track), subsection 9I.5 (PLAS), item 10 of 14.

## What
Add frankensqlite-backed witness/index stores with conformance tests for deterministic witness retrieval and replay joins.

## Detailed Requirements
1. Storage schema:
   - Witness table: stores full capability_witness artifacts with content-addressable primary key, indexed by extension_id, policy_id, epoch_id, lifecycle state, and promotion timestamp.
   - Index tables: per-capability lookup (which witnesses reference a given capability), per-extension history (witness version chain), escrow-event linkage.
   - Replay-join support: queries that join witness state with escrow/deny/grant receipts for a given extension and time window.
2. Deterministic retrieval:
   - Identical query inputs produce identical result ordering (stable sort by content hash or sequence number).
   - Pagination support with deterministic cursor semantics.
3. Conformance tests:
   - Verify round-trip: store witness, retrieve by each index, verify byte-identical.
   - Verify replay joins: store witness + receipts, query joined results, verify correctness.
   - Verify determinism: same sequence of operations produces identical database state regardless of timing.
   - Verify schema migration: older data remains queryable after schema upgrades.
4. Performance requirements:
   - Witness lookup by extension_id + epoch: sub-millisecond on typical deployment sizes.
   - Replay join queries: bounded latency with appropriate indexing.
5. All storage operations must use /dp/frankensqlite integration patterns from 10.14.

## Rationale
From 10.15: "Add frankensqlite-backed witness/index stores and conformance tests for deterministic witness retrieval and replay joins." Persistent storage of witnesses and indexes is essential for runtime capability enforcement (fast lookup), operator surfaces (queryable history), and audit (replay joins). Using frankensqlite ensures consistency with the project's persistence architecture.

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: CRUD operations on each table, index query correctness, replay-join correctness.
- Conformance tests: deterministic retrieval, round-trip fidelity, schema migration.
- Performance tests: latency benchmarks for critical query patterns at target data volumes.
- Stress tests: concurrent read/write patterns to verify SQLite locking behavior.

## Implementation Notes
- Use /dp/frankensqlite for all database operations; consider /dp/sqlmodel_rust for typed model layers where beneficial.
- Schema design should support efficient witness lifecycle queries (e.g., "all active witnesses for extensions in production").
- Consider write-ahead log mode for concurrent read performance.

## Dependencies
- bd-2w9w (witness schema defines the stored data structure).
- 10.14 (frankensqlite integration patterns).
- /dp/frankensqlite (storage framework).
- /dp/sqlmodel_rust (optional typed model layer).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Implement the full objective with deterministic behavior, explicit failure semantics, and safe fallback/rollback rules.
- Add focused unit tests for normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
- Add integration and/or end-to-end test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions, degraded mode, and recovery behavior with deterministic fixtures.
- Emit structured logs with stable keys (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and assert critical events in tests.
- Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, evidence pointers, replay pointers, benchmark/check outputs) plus clear operator verification steps.
- Ensure heavy Rust build/test execution paths are documented and run through rch wrappers when implementation begins.

title: [AUDIT-FUZZ] capability: missing fuzz target for CapabilityProfile deserialize
description:
File: crates/franken-engine/src/capability.rs:218-240
Target function: impl<'de> serde::Deserialize<'de> for CapabilityProfile::deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
Reachability: capability profiles are policy/manifest-facing authority data; attacker-controlled or corrupted JSON can reach serde_json::from_str::<CapabilityProfile> before validate_canonical rejects smuggled grants.
Attack surface: arbitrary JSON objects with kind/capabilities fields, duplicate/unknown capability strings, huge arrays, mixed casing, missing fields, and nested malformed values.
Failure modes that would be valuable to fuzz:
  - capability-smuggling wrong-result where a non-canonical capability set deserializes successfully
  - panic or stack blowup on deeply nested/malformed JSON
  - OOM from oversized capabilities arrays or repeated duplicate grants
  - acceptance drift for unknown capabilities, aliases, or profile kinds
Suggested harness: structure-aware JSON via arbitrary::Arbitrary for bounded RawProfile-like inputs plus a raw UTF-8 JSON mode; call serde_json::from_slice::<CapabilityProfile>(data) and assert every Ok result exactly equals one of the five canonical profiles.
Example invocation: cargo +nightly fuzz run capability_profile_deserialize -- -max_total_time=300
close_reason: done: added fuzz target capability_profile_deserialize, validates security invariant that all deserialized profiles match canonical definitions, prevents capability smuggling via JSON manipulation

title: [SWARM-CTRL-G] Add deterministic stress fixtures for resource-pressure decisions
description:
## What
Add deterministic stress and replay fixtures for the resource governor and validation planner under CPU, memory, disk, `rch`, and coordination pressure scenarios.

## Why
A control plane for large swarms is only useful if it fails predictably when the machine is noisy. These fixtures should prevent regressions where missing telemetry is misread as healthy or broad validation sneaks back into the path.

## How
- Build fixture inputs rather than spawning real resource exhaustion.
- Cover active cargo/rustc counts, low disk, unwritable target dir, missing `rch`, `rch` local fallback, Agent Mail unavailable, reserved-file overlap, stale proof evidence, and unknown path mappings.
- Pair each fixture with expected decision JSON/goldens and detailed logs explaining the remediation.

## Risks
- Simulated pressure that does not match production signals.
- Non-deterministic timestamps or host paths in goldens.
- Fixtures that only test happy paths.

## Success Criteria
- Golden outputs are stable across repeated runs.
- Each pressure scenario maps to a visible `defer`, `admit_narrow`, or `fail_closed` decision.
- Test logs include enough context to debug a failed swarm run without rerunning interactively.

With allow_development_trust=true, an unsigned development manifest with a tampered content_hash is accepted, letting dev-trust provenance artifacts carry an identity hash that does not bind the canonical manifest bytes. Require content_hash to match canonical bytes for development manifests too, while still preserving the explicit allow_development_trust override for unsigned manifests, and add regression coverage.

title: [CRITICAL][REVIEW] Cold-start runtime image manifest marks synthetic demo hashes verified
description:
Reality-check scope: runtime_image_contract.rs and cold-start runtime-image bundle versus reproducible/signed runtime artifact claims.

Docs/claims:
- AGENTS.md requires significant claims to have reproducible artifacts.
- docs/RGC_COLD_START_COMPILATION_LANE_V1.md:34-51 says runtime_image_manifest.json is a bundle artifact preserving enough detail for replay, differential triage, and operator forensics.
- docs/SEMANTIC_DONOR_SPEC.md:122 says signed runtime artifacts carrying epoch metadata require verifier-supplied current epoch/frontier and validity-window checks.

Reality gap:
crates/franken-engine/src/cold_start_compilation_lane.rs builds the runtime_image_manifest from demo labels rather than persisted runtime image bytes. evaluate_default_artifacts() fixes epoch to 42 and build_demo_entrygraphs() emits demo graphs. build_runtime_image_manifest() registers img-prewarmed-demo/img-zygote-demo/img-aot-demo with image_hash = hash_label("img-...-demo") and integrity_status = ImageIntegrityStatus::Verified. hash_label() is just ContentHash::compute(label.as_bytes()). No actual runtime image artifact is written/read, no image bytes are hashed, and no signature/validity window/frontier is verified.

Concrete audit commands:
```bash
nl -ba crates/franken-engine/src/cold_start_compilation_lane.rs | sed -n "280,303p;389,436p;476,548p;740,742p"
nl -ba docs/RGC_COLD_START_COMPILATION_LANE_V1.md | sed -n "32,51p"
nl -ba docs/SEMANTIC_DONOR_SPEC.md | sed -n "121,123p"
```

Impact: the cold-start lane can publish runtime_image_manifest.json that looks verified and replay-forensic but is backed by synthetic label hashes, not real image content. This is a CRITICAL proof-honesty gap because operators can treat fake/demo runtime-image evidence as shipped proof.

Acceptance: either wire the manifest to real persisted runtime image artifacts and hash/sign the actual bytes with epoch/frontier acceptance checks, or mark this artifact path explicitly synthetic/provisional and exclude it from proof/release claims until real image evidence exists.
close_reason: shipped: cold-start runtime image manifests now mark demo label-hash entries as PROVISIONAL_SYNTHETIC, release_claim_eligible=false, disabled/unverified images, documented proof limitations, and runner jq checks preventing synthetic Verified proof claims. Commit a9e1afb9. Validation: cargo fmt -p frankenengine-engine --check PASS; RCH cargo check -p frankenengine-engine failed before compiler execution twice with selection error: queue_timeout / remote required no worker assigned.

title: EPIC: Developer Experience and Documentation Improvements
description:
Supporting findings from modes-of-reasoning analysis -- identified by Perspective-Taking I4, Debiasing L2, Scope-Control L5.

## Problem

1. No onboarding path for human contributors (I4): No CONTRIBUTING.md, no architecture diagram, no module dependency graph. The project is optimized for AI agents (AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md) but humans have nothing. An experienced Rust developer would need 2-3 days of focused reading to orient. A typical contributor would be lost for a week.

2. README bloat (L5): The README is ~2,260 lines. Lines 1-200 are useful (description, quick start, design philosophy). Lines 200-2150 are ~1,950 lines documenting individual gate scripts, artifact paths, and replay commands -- an operator runbook disguised as a README.

3. No Test262 conformance reporting (I4 + L2): The most important metric for a JavaScript runtime does not exist. The project reports 37,897+ internal tests but no external conformance numbers. Even a low Test262 pass rate would be more credible than silence.

4. AI reasoning artifacts in production code (I4): evidence_ledger.rs contains agent reasoning traces ("Assume it has major() and minor()... We will use a hack"). These undermine confidence in code quality during security audits.

5. Novel vocabulary obscures standard concepts (L5): "Dark matter saturation" = untested paths. "Galaxy-brain explainability" = decision explanation. "Moonshot contract" = stretch goal. Custom terminology where standard names exist creates unnecessary cognitive load.

## Key Files
- README.md (restructure)
- CONTRIBUTING.md (create)
- docs/ (162 documents -- need index/overview)
- crates/franken-engine/src/evidence_ledger.rs (AI artifacts)

## Success Criteria
- 2-page architecture overview showing parse->lower->execute pipeline and IR levels
- README restructured to ~300 lines with links to ops/ for gate docs
- Test262 runner integrated, pass rate published (even if low)
- AI reasoning artifacts audited and removed from all source files
- CONTRIBUTING.md exists with clear onboarding path
close_reason: done: All child beads completed. Architecture overview (bd-axlvk.1) created docs/ARCHITECTURE_OVERVIEW.md. README restructured (bd-axlvk.2). Test262 conformance runner integrated (bd-axlvk.3). AI reasoning artifacts audited and removed (bd-axlvk.4). CONTRIBUTING.md created with human onboarding (bd-axlvk.5). Epic objectives achieved: human contributor onboarding path established, documentation improved, code quality enhanced.

title: [deadlock-finder] Add process-wide lock for shadow decision artifact bundles
description: deadlock-finder audit found a concrete multi-process race in crates/franken-engine/src/shadow_decision_composer.rs. write_shadow_decision_artifacts serializes writers with a static LazyLock<Mutex<BTreeMap<PathBuf, Arc<Mutex<()>>>>> but that only protects writers inside one process. The function writes a multi-file bundle where shadow_status.json is the completion signal; two frankenctl/script processes targeting the same output_dir can still interleave operator_notice/events/commands/report/recommendations/shadow_status writes and publish a mixed bundle. Fix by taking a filesystem advisory lock under the output directory for the whole bundle write, while keeping the in-process lock. Use existing rustix fs flock support; do not delete the lock file on release. Add a focused regression for lock contention and source-level validation.
notes: Implemented source change in crates/franken-engine/src/shadow_decision_composer.rs: write_shadow_decision_artifacts now takes a persistent output-dir advisory flock for the whole multi-file bundle, while retaining the process-local mutex. Added unit regression output_dir_file_lock_blocks_second_writer_until_release. Source-level validation passed: rustix 1.1.4 exposes flock<Fd: AsFd>(fd, FlockOperation) and FlockOperation::{LockExclusive,NonBlockingLockExclusive,Unlock}; cargo fmt --check --manifest-path crates/franken-engine/Cargo.toml passed; git diff --check passed. Cargo validation blocked: both timeout 900 rch exec -- env CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTFLAGS='-C linker=cc' cargo test -p frankenengine-engine ... attempts exited 124 with no compiler diagnostic after reaching frankenengine-test-support compilation.
close_reason: Revalidated after support-heavy integration tests were isolated. Output reached the test result without compiling frankenengine-test-support: Finished test profile in 22m 16s; running 1 test; shadow_decision_composer::tests::output_dir_file_lock_blocks_second_writer_until_release ... ok; test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 40364 filtered out. cargo fmt --check passed. title: [AUDIT-DETERMINISM] react_compilation_pipeline::compile_react_source uses SystemTime::now()
description:
File: crates/franken-engine/src/react_compilation_pipeline.rs:284-287
Documented invariant (AGENTS.md): "deterministic replay and auditable decision artifacts"
Code excerpt:
```
timestamp: std::time::SystemTime::now()
    .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
    .unwrap_or_default()
    .as_secs(),
```
Why this is a bug: ReactCompileMetadata.timestamp is populated from wall-clock, making compile-output metadata non-deterministic across replays of the same source. Violates AGENTS.md determinism rule and the "Significant claims require reproducible artifacts" non-negotiable architectural constraint.
Reachability: any caller of compile_react_source() (production React/JSX compile pipeline).
Repro / detection: compile the same source twice in different seconds, observe metadata.timestamp differs.
Suggested fix: Add a deterministic clock parameter to ReactCompileConfig (e.g., `compile_epoch: SecurityEpoch`) and have callers thread the epoch through. Or remove the timestamp field from ReactCompileMetadata if not load-bearing for any consumer (the only existing assertion is `assert!(timestamp > 0)` which can be replaced with a structural check).
Note: Found while reviewing tree-fix work in this session — pre-existing bug, not introduced by 8a09353e/a06be4fd.
close_reason: Replaced wall-clock React compile metadata with deterministic compile_epoch and added focused integration regression coverage; focused rch React pipeline test passed, all-targets check hit rch SSH timeout before completion.

title: [11] Evidence And Decision Contracts (Mandatory) - Comprehensive Execution Epic
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 11: Evidence And Decision Contracts (Mandatory).

## What
Governance epic ensuring all high-impact subsystem work is packaged as explicit decision contracts with required evidence fields and reproducibility hooks. This section operationalizes the rule: no contract, no merge.

## Rationale
FrankenEngine makes high-stakes claims (security, determinism, category-shift performance). Without mandatory contract structure, those claims devolve into unverifiable narratives. This epic turns decision quality into enforceable engineering policy.

## Contract Scope
Every qualifying change must carry:
- change summary
- hotspot/threat evidence
- EV score and tier
- expected-loss model
- fallback trigger
- rollout wedge
- rollback command
- benchmark and correctness artifacts

## Dependency Model
This epic should gate section epics whose outputs produce program claims (`13`, `14`, `15`, `16`) and remain aligned with the 10.x execution master for implementation evidence production.

## Validation Model
- Contract completeness checks are deterministic and CI-enforceable.
- Unit/e2e verification and structured logging requirements are mandatory on child work.
- Reproducibility artifacts must be present and operator-runnable.

## Success Criteria
1. All child beads are complete with contract-complete, artifact-backed evidence.
2. Missing-contract work is prevented from reaching completion states.
3. Dependency graph remains acyclic and reflects real gate ordering.
4. Contract outputs are sufficient for independent replay and operator audit.
acceptance_criteria:
1. All child beads for this epic must be completed with artifact-backed evidence and no unresolved critical blockers.
2. Every child implementation bead must include comprehensive unit tests plus deterministic integration/end-to-end test scripts that validate normal, boundary, failure, and adversarial behavior.
3. Child test suites must assert structured logging for critical events (`trace_id`, `decision_id`, `policy_id`, `component`, `event`, `outcome`, `error_code`) and include operator-readable diagnostics.
4. Reproducibility artifacts must be attached or linked for each closed child (`env/manifest`, replay/evidence pointers, verification commands, and benchmark/check outputs where applicable).
5. Dependency structure must remain acyclic, executable in order, and reflect real implementation sequencing (no false-ready milestones).
6. Epic closure is allowed only when plan scope is fully preserved (no feature/functionality loss versus referenced PLAN section) and rollback/fallback behavior is documented.\n7. For any CPU-intensive Rust build/test/benchmark workflow under this epic, require documented or executed `rch` wrappers.
close_reason: Closed Section 11 evidence-and-decision contracts epic after verifying all 10 listed dependencies are closed, including the 10.x master gate, and br dep cycles reports zero cycles. Closeout-only: no source changes; downstream Section 12/13/14 epics remain separate follow-on work.

title: [review][extension_host_topology_assessment] Frame topology assessment content hash inputs
description: Review finding from commit 4c31aba7 in crates/franken-engine/src/extension_host_topology_assessment.rs. TopologyPromotionAssessment::compute_content_hash at lines 275-323 feeds variable-length strings, vectors, and numeric fields directly into one Sha256 stream without field tags, collection boundaries, or length prefixes. Distinct operator-visible assessments can therefore produce the same preimage stream, for example source_files ["ab", "c"] versus ["a", "bc"], or similar boundary shifts across rationale, evidence, benefits, risks, and implementation_order. The content_hash is emitted as the assessment identity and then consumed by the Asupersync adoption gate, so ambiguous hashing weakens replay and artifact integrity. Fix by hashing a domain-separated canonical encoding with field tags and length prefixes, or canonical serde over the full assessment with content_hash cleared, and add a regression test for a boundary-collision pair.
close_reason: done: Fixed content hash boundary collisions by replacing direct SHA256 concatenation with canonical JSON serialization. Added comprehensive regression tests for boundary collision scenarios. Prevents distinct assessments from producing identical hashes.

title: [REVIEW] Critical determinism regression in shadow replay verifier
description: CRITICAL: shadow_replay_verifier.rs:662 and :786 switched from deterministic_serde::to_canonical_bytes to serde_json::to_vec in commit 733f1423. This breaks replay determinism guarantee - JSON field ordering is not guaranteed, making behavioral regression detection unreliable. title: [SWARM-CTRL] Build rch-aware validation control plane for large agent swarms
description:
## Background
FrankenEngine is now being worked by multiple agents at once, and the high-value proof/build/test lanes already rely on `rch`, bead state, proof artifacts, Agent Mail coordination, and focused shell gates. The project needs a first-class control plane for this: something that turns many concurrent agents and a large machine into predictable throughput instead of hidden compile pressure, stale proof claims, and duplicate validation work.

This epic is plan-space for a practical, repo-native swarm validation control plane. It should stay aligned with AGENTS.md: Rust/Cargo only, no destructive filesystem behavior, no `master` references, reusable sibling repos where appropriate, and significant claims backed by reproducible artifacts.

## Goals
- Make large multi-agent sessions faster by planning focused `rch` validation instead of broad cargo churn.
- Make resource use safer by admitting or deferring local/remote work based on explicit CPU, memory, disk, and `rch` fallback signals.
- Make proof evidence easier to inspect by indexing command receipts, artifact manifests, bead IDs, source revisions, and gate outcomes.
- Make operator status readable without requiring manual correlation across `br`, Agent Mail, logs, and artifacts.
- Preserve deterministic replay and fail-closed behavior: uncertain capacity or stale evidence should degrade to a bounded, visible safe mode.

## Non-Goals
- Do not build a parallel task tracker to replace `br`/`bv`.
- Do not build a bespoke TUI framework; reuse `/dp/frankentui` for advanced console surfaces if the work goes beyond machine-readable reports.
- Do not hard-code frankensqlite WAL/PRAGMA/migration policy locally; typed persistence work should route through `/dp/frankensqlite` and `/dp/sqlmodel_rust` where schema layers are beneficial.
- Do not introduce background deletion or cleanup behavior.

## Success Criteria

title: Performance regression in Number.toString radix conversion
description:
The Number.toString radix conversion implementation in commit f433744d has O(n²) performance due to inefficient string building.

ISSUE: Lines 11690-11697 use result.insert(0, char) inside a loop, causing quadratic performance.

Each insert(0) shifts all existing characters, making total complexity O(n²) where n is the number of digits.

IMPACT:
- Severe performance degradation for large numbers
- Potential DoS via Number.toString(2) on large numbers  
- Regression from previous placeholder implementation

SOLUTION:
- Build digits in reverse order, then reverse once
- Or use Vec<char> and collect into String

LOCATION: crates/franken-engine/src/baseline_interpreter.rs:11693-11697
close_reason: fixed: Replaced O(n²) string building with efficient Vec<char> approach. Changed from repeated result.insert(0, char) to building digits in Vec and reversing them, reducing complexity from O(n²) to O(n). Also added capacity pre-allocation for better performance.

title: [10.2] Define parser trait + canonical AST invariants for ES2020 script/module goals.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.2, item 1. Cross-refs: 9A.1, 9B.1, 9F.4, Phase A exit gate.

## What
Define the parser trait interface and canonical AST type hierarchy for ES2020 script and module goal symbols. This is the foundation of the entire compilation pipeline - IR0 (SyntaxIR) is produced by this layer.

## Detailed Requirements
- Parser trait must be generic over input source (string, stream, file) with deterministic error reporting
- AST nodes must be canonical: structurally identical source produces identical AST (no parse-order-dependent metadata)
- Must support both Script and Module goal symbols per ES2020 spec
- AST must carry source location spans for error reporting and debugging
- AST serialization must be deterministic for replay/hash purposes (canonical serialization invariant from plan)
- Must NOT mirror V8 or QuickJS internal AST structures - this is a de novo design informed by observable ES2020 semantics (per Section 10.1 donor-extraction policy)

## Rationale
The plan's multi-level IR stack (IR0→IR4) starts here. Without a well-defined parser trait and canonical AST, nothing downstream can be deterministic. The 9F.4 Capability-Typed TS Execution Contract requires that capability intent be traceable from source through all IR levels. This means the AST must be designed to support downstream capability annotation, not retrofitted later.

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests: parse valid ES2020 script/module sources, verify AST structure matches expected canonical form
- Unit tests: parse invalid sources, verify deterministic error with source location
- Unit tests: verify canonical serialization (same source → same serialized AST bytes)
- Property tests: round-trip parse → serialize → parse produces identical AST
- Conformance: test262 parse-only subset as baseline validation
- Edge cases: empty source, unicode identifiers, nested template literals, destructuring patterns

## Implementation Notes
- Define in crates/franken-engine as core parser trait
- Consider arena allocation for AST nodes (9B.1 recommends arena allocation for IR nodes)
- AST node types should be exhaustive enum, not trait objects, for determinism and performance
- Hash invariant: define canonical hash over AST for use in IR0 witness artifacts

## Dependencies
- Blocks: IR contract (bd-1wa), lowering pipelines (bd-ug9), interpreter skeleton (bd-2f8)
- Blocked by: nothing (foundational)

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid/adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end/integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds/fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (`trace_id`, `decision_id`, `policy_id`, `component`, `event`, `outcome`, `error_code`) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build/test workflows introduced by this bead, document/execute via `rch`-wrapped commands for heavy compilation/test workloads.

title: [10.12] Add counterexample synthesizer for conflicting policy controllers and ambiguous merges.
description:
## Plan Reference
- **10.12 Item 12** (Counterexample synthesizer for policy conflicts)
- **9H.5**: Policy Theorem Engine -> canonical owner: 9F.8 (Policy Compiler With Formal Merge Guarantees), execution: 10.12
- **9F.8**: Policy Compiler With Formal Merge Guarantees -- on conflict, compiler emits bounded counterexample traces and deterministic rejection diagnostics

## What
Build a counterexample synthesizer that, when the policy theorem compiler detects conflicting policy controllers or ambiguous merges, automatically generates minimal concrete counterexample traces demonstrating the conflict. These traces serve as actionable diagnostics for policy authors and as regression test fixtures.

## Detailed Requirements

### Counterexample Synthesis
1. **Trigger conditions**: The synthesizer activates when any policy compiler pass (from bd-3oc) reports a property violation:
   - Monotonicity violation: a composition path amplifies authority
   - Non-interference violation: policy evaluation leaks cross-domain information
   - Merge non-determinism: different merge orderings produce different results
   - Precedence ambiguity: two policies have incomparable priority in some evaluation context
   - Attenuation violation: delegated authority exceeds delegator's envelope
2. **Counterexample format**: Structured artifact containing:
   - `conflict_id`: Unique identifier for this conflict instance
   - `property_violated`: Which formal property failed
   - `policy_ids[]`: The policies involved in the conflict
   - `merge_path`: The specific composition sequence that triggers the conflict
   - `concrete_scenario`: A minimal set of inputs (subjects, capabilities, conditions) that demonstrates the violation
   - `expected_outcome`: What the correct outcome should be under the violated property
   - `actual_outcome`: What the conflicting composition actually produces
   - `minimality_evidence`: Proof that the counterexample is minimal (no proper subset triggers the same violation)
3. **Minimization**: Synthesizer uses delta-debugging or similar shrinking to reduce counterexamples to the smallest concrete scenario that still demonstrates the violation.

### Synthesis Strategies
1. **SMT-driven synthesis**: For properties checked via SMT (from bd-3oc), extract counterexample models directly from the solver's satisfying assignment.
2. **Enumeration-based synthesis**: For simpler properties, enumerate candidate scenarios from policy rule combinations and test property violations.
3. **Mutation-based synthesis**: Start from known-good policy compositions; mutate merge orderings, priority assignments, and condition parameters to discover violations.
4. **Timeout-bounded**: Synthesis has a configurable compute budget (default: 30s). On timeout, emit partial counterexample with `{status: incomplete, best_candidate, search_coverage}`.

### Output Integration
1. **Developer diagnostics**: Counterexamples are rendered as human-readable policy conflict reports with highlighted conflict points, affected subjects/capabilities, and suggested resolution strategies.
2. **Regression corpus**: Each counterexample is automatically added to the policy regression test corpus. Future policy changes must not re-introduce resolved conflicts.
3. **Replay integration**: Counterexample scenarios are formatted as deterministic replay fixtures that the replay engine (bd-1nh) can execute.
4. **Audit trail**: Counterexample generation events are logged to the evidence ledger with: `conflict_id`, `synthesis_strategy`, `compute_time`, `minimality_depth`, and `resolution_status`.

### Multi-Controller Conflict Detection
1. When multiple policy controllers affect overlapping metrics or decision surfaces, the synthesizer specifically tests for:
   - **Interference**: Controller A's adjustments invalidate Controller B's invariants.
   - **Oscillation**: Controllers produce cyclic adjustments that never converge.
   - **Timescale conflict**: Controllers operating at different timescales produce inconsistent intermediate states.
2. Required timescale-separation statements (per 10.13) are validated: if two controllers lack sufficient timescale separation, synthesizer generates scenarios demonstrating potential interference.

## Rationale
> "On conflict, compiler emits bounded counterexample traces and deterministic rejection diagnostics." -- 9F.8
> "Large teams can safely compose many policy sources without hidden privilege escalations or merge-order bugs. Policy evolution becomes disciplined engineering, not textual patching." -- 9F.8

Counterexamples transform abstract property violations into concrete, actionable evidence. Without them, policy authors face opaque "merge failed" errors; with them, they see exactly what went wrong and how to fix it.

## Testing Requirements
1. **Unit tests**: Synthesis for each property violation type with known-conflicting policies; minimization correctness (verify counterexample is actually minimal); timeout behavior with partial results.
2. **Property tests**: Generate random policy pairs; if compiler detects violation, verify synthesizer produces valid counterexample that actually demonstrates the violation; if compiler finds no violation, verify synthesizer does not produce spurious counterexamples.
3. **Integration tests**: Full pipeline from conflicting policy submission through compiler detection, counterexample synthesis, diagnostic rendering, and regression corpus addition.
4. **Performance tests**: Synthesis latency distribution for various conflict complexity levels; memory usage under large policy spaces.
5. **Regression tests**: Library of known policy conflicts (real-world-inspired scenarios); verify synthesizer produces counterexamples for each.

## Implementation Notes
- Synthesizer module extends the policy compiler infrastructure (bd-3oc) with counterexample extraction.
- SMT model extraction should wrap the Z3 model API to produce structured counterexamples.
- Minimization uses iterative shrinking with deterministic ordering for reproducibility.
- Human-readable diagnostic rendering should support both terminal output and structured JSON.
- Regression corpus management: append-only with deduplication by `conflict_id`.

## Dependencies
- bd-3oc: Policy theorem compiler passes (synthesizer extends compiler diagnostics)

title: [10.7] Integrate transplanted extension conformance assets into runnable suites.
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.7 (Conformance + Verification), item 1.
Related: Phase A exit gate (baseline conformance passes), 10.1 (feature-parity tracker wired to test262/lockstep/waiver governance), 10.5 (Extension Host + Security).

## What
Integrate transplanted extension conformance assets -- test fixtures, expected-output baselines, edge-case vectors, and harness scaffolding harvested from donor runtimes (QuickJS, reference implementations) during the semantic-donor extraction process -- into runnable, CI-gated conformance suites within the FrankenEngine test infrastructure.

## Detailed Requirements
1. **Asset inventory manifest:** Produce a machine-readable manifest (`conformance_assets.json`) listing every transplanted asset with fields: `source_donor`, `semantic_domain` (e.g., `promise_resolution`, `proxy_trap_ordering`, `module_namespace_binding`), `normative_reference` (ES2020 clause), `fixture_hash`, `expected_output_hash`, and `import_date`.
2. **Harness adapter layer:** Implement a thin adapter that maps donor-specific harness conventions (e.g., `$262.createRealm`, `$DONE`, `print()`) to FrankenEngine's native test driver API without introducing behavioral shims that could mask semantic divergence.
3. **Deterministic runner:** Each suite file executes under a deterministic seed, fixed locale/timezone, and reproducible GC schedule. Non-determinism must cause hard failure, never silent skip.
4. **Output canonicalization:** Normalize floating-point formatting, error message strings, and property enumeration order to canonical form before comparison, with explicit documentation of each normalization rule and its ES2020 justification.
5. **Waiver file integration:** Any asset that cannot pass must have an entry in the central waiver file (`conformance_waivers.toml`) with fields: `asset_id`, `reason_code` (enum: `harness_gap | host_hook_missing | intentional_divergence | not_yet_implemented`), `tracking_bead`, `expiry_date`. Zero silent failures policy: unwaived failures block CI.
6. **Structured logging:** Emit per-asset structured log lines with fields: `trace_id`, `asset_id`, `semantic_domain`, `outcome` (pass|fail|waived|error), `duration_us`, `error_code`, `error_detail`.
7. **Evidence artifact:** Each CI run produces a `conformance_evidence.jsonl` bundle linking run manifest, asset manifest hash, pass/fail/waiver counts, and environment fingerprint for reproducibility contract compliance.

## Rationale
Transplanted conformance assets represent the highest-fidelity record of donor-runtime semantic behavior. Failing to integrate them into runnable suites means the extraction investment is wasted and semantic drift between FrankenEngine and the donor behavioral specification goes undetected. This is the foundational layer upon which all other 10.7 verification beads build.

## Testing Requirements (Meta-Tests for Test Infrastructure)
1. **Harness-fidelity meta-test:** Verify the adapter layer produces identical outputs to the donor harness for a reference subset (>= 50 assets) by running both and diffing canonicalized output.
2. **Waiver enforcement meta-test:** Inject a synthetic unwaived failure and confirm CI blocks. Inject a waived failure and confirm CI passes with waiver logged.
3. **Non-determinism detection meta-test:** Run the same asset 10x under identical seed and confirm bitwise-identical output; run under a different seed and confirm the harness detects the difference.
4. **Manifest integrity meta-test:** Tamper with one asset file and confirm the manifest hash check fails before execution begins.
5. **Evidence artifact schema meta-test:** Validate `conformance_evidence.jsonl` against a JSON Schema and confirm all required fields are present and non-empty.

## Implementation Notes
- Transplanted assets live under `tests/conformance/transplanted/` with subdirectories per semantic domain.
- The adapter layer is a Rust module (`crate::test_harness::donor_adapter`) that implements `DonorHarnessApi` trait.
- Runner integrates with `rch`-wrapped compilation/test workflows for heavy workloads.
- Waiver file is shared with bd-11p (test262 integration) to maintain a single source of truth for conformance exceptions.

## Dependencies
- Upstream: 10.1 (donor-extraction scope document, feature-parity tracker), 10.2 (VM Core parser/evaluator must exist to run assets).
- Downstream: bd-11p (test262 integration builds on this harness), bd-2rk (probabilistic security conformance reuses runner infrastructure), all other 10.7 beads consume the evidence artifact format.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.

title: [10.9] Release gate: proof-specialized lanes demonstrate positive performance delta versus ambient-authority lanes with 100% specialization-receipt coverage and deterministic fallback correctness (implementation ownership: `10.12` + `10.15` + `10.6` + `10.7`).
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.9, item 9 -- Moonshot Disruption Track (release gates for frontier programs).

## What
This is a **release gate**, not an implementation task. It verifies that proof-specialized lanes -- built collaboratively by the Frontier Programs track (10.12), Delta Moonshots track (10.15), Performance Program (10.6), and Conformance track (10.7) -- demonstrate a positive performance delta versus ambient-authority lanes, with 100% specialization-receipt coverage and deterministic fallback correctness. This is the most cross-cutting gate in Section 10.9, validating that the convergence of proof-carrying code, capability-typed execution, and performance optimization yields measurable real-world improvement.

The gate owner does not build the proof-specialized lanes; the gate owner benchmarks them against ambient-authority lanes, audits receipt coverage, and validates fallback behavior.

## Gate Criteria
1. Proof-specialized lanes achieve a positive performance delta (wall-time, throughput, or memory -- at least one, ideally all) versus ambient-authority lanes on the canonical benchmark corpus, with statistical significance (p < 0.05).
2. 100% specialization-receipt coverage: every optimization decision in a proof-specialized lane is backed by a signed specialization receipt containing: optimization name, proof reference, capability witness reference, pre/post performance measurement, and receipt signature.
3. Deterministic fallback correctness: when a proof-specialized lane encounters a case where specialization cannot be applied (e.g., proof generation fails, capability is revoked), it falls back to the ambient-authority path and produces correct output with a structured fallback receipt.
4. Fallback behavior is tested with deliberately injected proof failures and capability revocations; the lane never crashes, hangs, or produces incorrect output.
5. Performance measurements use the same harness and methodology as the Node/Bun comparison gate (bd-1ze) to ensure comparability.
6. Receipt chain for a full proof-specialized compilation is replayable end-to-end: an independent operator can verify the entire specialization decision history from receipts alone.

## Implementation Ownership
- **10.12 (Frontier Programs):** Builds the proof-carrying optimization infrastructure and specialization runtime. Encompasses 9F moonshots: Verified Adaptive Compiler, Cryptographic Receipts, SLO-Proven Scheduler, Semantic Build Graph.
- **10.15 (Delta Moonshots):** Builds capability-typed execution, PLAS integration, and specialization receipt signing. Encompasses 9I moonshots: Security-Proof-Guided Specialization, TEE-Bound Receipts, PLAS.
- **10.6 (Performance Program):** Provides performance benchmarking infrastructure, regression detection, and statistical analysis tooling.
- **10.7 (Conformance + Verification):** Provides receipt verification infrastructure, conformance test suites, and fallback correctness validation.
- **10.9 (this gate):** Orchestrates the cross-track evaluation, benchmarks proof-specialized vs ambient-authority lanes, audits receipt coverage, validates fallback behavior, and certifies the evidence bundle.

## Rationale
This gate is the culmination of FrankenEngine's core thesis: that proof-carrying, capability-typed execution can be not just safer but also faster than ambient-authority execution. If proof-specialized lanes are slower than ambient-authority lanes, the entire moonshot narrative collapses -- security and correctness guarantees become costs rather than enablers. By requiring positive performance delta with 100% receipt coverage, this gate proves that the security overhead is not just tolerable but actually enables optimizations that ambient-authority code cannot safely perform. This gate feeds all three dimensions of the disruption scorecard (bd-6pk): `performance_delta` (positive delta), `security_delta` (receipt-backed proof chain), and `autonomy_delta` (self-specializing optimization).

Related 9F moonshots: Verified Adaptive Compiler, Cryptographic Receipts, SLO-Proven Scheduler, Semantic Build Graph, Autopilot Perf Scientist.
Related 9I moonshots: Security-Proof-Guided Specialization, TEE-Bound Receipts, PLAS.

## Verification Requirements
- **Performance benchmark:** Run the canonical benchmark corpus on both proof-specialized and ambient-authority lanes under identical conditions; confirm positive delta with p < 0.05.
- **Receipt coverage audit:** Enumerate all specialization decisions in a representative compilation; confirm 100% receipt coverage with no gaps.
- **Receipt chain replay:** An independent operator replays the full receipt chain for a representative compilation; confirm all receipts verify and the chain is complete.
- **Fallback injection testing:** Inject proof failures and capability revocations; confirm the lane falls back correctly, produces correct output, and emits fallback receipts.
- **Fallback performance:** Confirm fallback path performance is no worse than ambient-authority lane performance (fallback does not introduce a regression).
- **Cross-gate consistency:** Confirm performance measurements are consistent with the Node/Bun comparison harness methodology (bd-1ze).
- **Scorecard integration:** Results feed all three dimensions of the disruption scorecard (bd-6pk).
- **Structured logging:** Proof-specialized lane runs emit structured logs with fields: `trace_id`, `lane_type` (proof-specialized/ambient-authority), `optimization_pass`, `proof_status`, `capability_witness_ref`, `specialization_receipt_hash`, `fallback_triggered`, `wall_time_ns`, `memory_peak_bytes`.

## Dependencies
- bd-6pk (disruption scorecard) -- gate results feed all three scorecard dimensions.
- bd-1ze (Node/Bun comparison harness gate) -- shares benchmark methodology and corpus.
- bd-2rx (proof-carrying optimization gate) -- proof-specialized lanes depend on the proof-carrying pipeline being enabled.
- bd-2n3 (PLAS gate) -- proof-specialized lanes require PLAS-granted capabilities for specialization.
- bd-181 (GA native lanes gate) -- proof-specialized lanes build on fully native GA lanes.
- 10.12 Frontier Programs track -- delivers proof-carrying optimization infrastructure.
- 10.15 Delta Moonshots track -- delivers capability-typed execution and receipt signing.
- 10.6 Performance Program -- delivers benchmarking infrastructure.
- 10.7 Conformance + Verification track -- delivers receipt verification and fallback conformance testing.
- bd-1xm (parent epic) -- this bead is a child of the Moonshot Disruption Track epic.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.

title: [CRITICAL] [REVIEW] Compromise-rate child gate can emit passing artifact from placeholder evidence
description:
Review finding from mock-code-finder sweep.

`crates/franken-engine/src/compromise_rate_disruptive_floor_metric_gate.rs` still carries production-path placeholder semantics after bd-1vwza/bd-1pc4e closure. `RuntimeDenominator::baseline_compromise_rate_millionths` has TODO placeholder Node/Bun rates at lines 33-38. More importantly, `analyze_compromise_rate_metric_input` marks fictional evidence as `data_quality = targeted`, but still computes `overall_outcome = pass` purely from placeholder reduction ratios at lines 497-510. `generate_compromise_rate_metric_artifact` then emits a parent-consumable `MetricArtifact` with observed reduction, confidence/coverage 950000, and a zero sha256 fallback if no valid output hash is present at lines 552-612. The parent disruptive-floor gate only sees `MetricArtifact` fields and has no data-quality/provisional flag, so targeted placeholder compromise evidence can look like observed proof.

Why this matters: AGENTS.md requires significant claims to have reproducible artifacts. A fabricated or targeted red-team proof must fail closed or be explicitly downgraded before it reaches `MetricArtifact`, not merely described in uncertainty notes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fictional/targeted compromise-rate evidence cannot produce a passing `MetricArtifact` accepted as observed disruptive-floor proof.
- Missing/invalid output hashes must fail closed rather than falling back to all-zero sha256 in a proof artifact.
- Placeholder default Node/Bun compromise rates are removed from production proof paths or isolated behind explicitly target-only APIs that cannot feed parent observed claims.
- Add child-gate and parent-gate regressions showing placeholder/fictional compromise evidence is downgraded or rejected.
- Focused validation: cargo test -p frankenengine-engine compromise_rate_disruptive_floor_metric_gate --lib plus disruptive_floor_metric_gate parent filter, using isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR.

title: [10.12] Define fleet immune-system message protocol for signed evidence, local confidence, and containment intent propagation.
description:
## Plan Reference
- **10.12 Item 5** (Fleet immune-system message protocol)
- **9H.2**: Fleet Immune System Consensus Plane -> canonical owner: 9F.2, execution: 10.12
- **9F.2**: Fleet-Scale Runtime Immune System -- distributed defense plane with signed evidence and deterministic convergence

## What
Define the wire protocol and message schema for the fleet-wide immune system, enabling nodes to exchange signed evidence atoms, local posterior risk deltas, and containment intent signals. This protocol is the communication substrate for fleet-scale collective defense.

## Detailed Requirements

### Message Types
1. **Evidence Packet**: Core information unit containing `trace_id`, `extension_id`, `evidence_hash`, `posterior_delta` (log-likelihood contribution), `policy_version`, `node_id`, `timestamp`, `signature`. Represents a single node's local observation about an extension's behavior.
2. **Containment Intent**: Decision signal containing `intent_id`, `extension_id`, `proposed_action` (sandbox / suspend / terminate / quarantine), `confidence_level`, `supporting_evidence_ids[]`, `policy_version`, `node_id`, `timestamp`, `signature`. Represents a node's recommendation for collective action.
3. **Quorum Checkpoint**: Aggregation marker containing `checkpoint_seq`, `epoch_id`, `participating_nodes[]`, `evidence_summary_hash`, `containment_decisions[]`, `quorum_signatures[]`. Represents fleet-level consensus at a point in time.
4. **Heartbeat/Liveness**: Periodic signal containing `node_id`, `policy_version`, `evidence_frontier_hash`, `local_health_summary`, `timestamp`, `signature`. Used for partition detection and freshness validation.

### Protocol Semantics
1. **Gossip dissemination**: Evidence packets and containment intents propagate via efficient gossip (fanout-based, bounded TTL, deduplication by `evidence_hash` / `intent_id`).
2. **Quorum checkpoints**: Periodic checkpoints aggregate fleet state; quorum threshold is configurable (default: majority of healthy nodes).
3. **Deterministic precedence**: When evidence or intents conflict, precedence rules are deterministic and based on: (a) monotonic sequence ordering, (b) severity ordering (higher-severity containment wins), (c) node-id tiebreaker. No random or timing-dependent resolution.
4. **Partition semantics**: Under network partition, each partition operates independently with degraded-mode policies (see bd-34l). Partition detection uses heartbeat absence with configurable timeout.
5. **Evidence accumulation**: Posterior deltas from multiple nodes combine additively in log-likelihood space. Fleet-wide posterior for an extension is the sum of all received evidence deltas.

### Message Encoding and Security
1. All messages use deterministic serialization (per 10.10 contract) with schema-hash prefix validation.
2. All messages are signed by the emitting node's signing key (per 10.10 split principal model).
3. Replay protection: monotonic per-node sequence numbers; receivers reject out-of-order or replayed messages.
4. Message authentication: per-session MAC on point-to-point channels; signature verification on gossip-received messages.
5. Bandwidth budget: protocol must operate within configurable bandwidth ceiling per node (default: <= 1 MB/s for fleet traffic at 100-node scale).

### Schema Extensibility
1. Protocol versioning with negotiation handshake on connection establishment.
2. Forward-compatible field extensibility: unknown fields are preserved (not stripped) during gossip forwarding.
3. Schema registry for message types with explicit deprecation policy.

## Rationale
> "Nodes emit evidence packets (trace_id, extension_id, evidence_hash, posterior_delta, policy_version). A fleet protocol (gossip plus quorum checkpoints) reconciles evidence, resolves conflicts with deterministic precedence, and propagates containment decisions with bounded convergence SLOs." -- 9F.2
> "Endpoint-local defense is structurally too slow for modern supply-chain attacks. A collective inference and action plane creates network effects for security: every incident increases fleet immunity, not just local hardening." -- 9F.2

The fleet immune-system protocol is the foundational communication layer that transforms local detection into collective defense. Without it, each node is an isolated defender, which is the failure mode FrankenEngine explicitly rejects.

## Testing Requirements
1. **Unit tests**: Message serialization/deserialization round-trips with golden vectors; signature verification for all message types; deterministic precedence resolution for conflicting evidence/intents; replay rejection.
2. **Property tests**: Fuzz message generation to stress deserialization and validation; verify precedence determinism under all conflict permutations.
3. **Integration tests**: Multi-node simulation (3+ nodes) exercising gossip propagation, evidence accumulation, quorum checkpoint formation, and containment decision convergence.
4. **Network tests**: Simulate partition scenarios, message loss, message reordering, and high-latency paths; verify deterministic degraded behavior.
5. **Performance tests**: Bandwidth measurement at target scale (100 nodes); convergence latency measurement for evidence propagation.

## Implementation Notes
- Protocol layer should be transport-agnostic (abstract over TCP, QUIC, or in-process channels for testing).
- Use 10.11 anti-entropy reconciliation primitives for evidence state convergence after partitions heal.
- Gossip implementation can leverage existing efficient gossip libraries or implement a simple protocol; keep it replaceable behind a trait boundary.
- Consider protobuf or canonical CBOR for wire encoding with deterministic ordering guarantees.

## Dependencies
- 10.10: Deterministic serialization, EngineObjectId, split principal key model, signature contracts
- 10.11: Anti-entropy reconciliation primitives, epoch model
- 10.5: Bayesian posterior updater (local evidence generation feeds into this protocol)
- Downstream: bd-34l (convergence + partition policy consumes this protocol)

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Enriched Self-Contained Context (Plan Sections 9F.2, 9C.2, 9D.2)

### Bandwidth and Partition Semantics

**Bandwidth Budget Rationale**: The 1 MB/s target at 100-node scale is derived from:
- Evidence packet size: ~1 KB per evidence atom (trace_id: 32B, extension_id: 32B, evidence_hash: 32B, posterior_delta: 64B fixed-point, policy_version: 8B, timestamp: 8B, signature: 64B, metadata: ~700B)
- Expected evidence rate: ~100 evidence atoms/sec per node under moderate extension load
- At 100 nodes: 100 * 100 * 1KB = 10 MB/s raw evidence generation
- Gossip fan-out of ~3 peers: each node sees ~3x its share = ~300 KB/s incoming
- With quorum checkpoints every 10s: ~10 KB checkpoint overhead
- Total: ~310 KB/s per node, rounded to 1 MB/s headroom target (3x safety margin)

**Partition Behavior**: When network partitions occur:
1. Nodes detect missing gossip heartbeats within bounded timeout (configurable, default 5s)
2. Partitioned nodes enter degraded containment mode: local evidence continues accumulating, local decisions remain active, but fleet-level confidence scores are frozen
3. Deterministic precedence rule: revoke > suspend > sandbox > allow. If any partition-side has emitted a revocation, it takes precedence when partitions heal
4. On partition heal: anti-entropy reconciliation (bd-2n6) converges evidence sets. Conflicting containment decisions resolved by deterministic precedence + highest-epoch-wins. Repair artifacts emitted for audit
5. SLO contract: convergence to consistent fleet state within 30s of partition heal (configurable)

**Why Deterministic Precedence Over Vector Clocks**: Vector clocks track causal ordering but don't encode safety semantics. For security containment, 'which action is safest?' matters more than 'which happened first.' Deterministic precedence (revoke > suspend > sandbox > allow) ensures the most conservative action always wins regardless of causal order. This eliminates time-of-check/time-of-use attacks exploiting clock disagreements.

### Message Types (Detailed)
1. **EvidencePacket**: Individual evidence atom from single node. Signed by originating node. Fields: trace_id, extension_id, evidence_hash, posterior_delta (fixed-point millionths for determinism), policy_version, epoch, signature.
2. **ContainmentIntent**: Node's proposed containment action. Fields: extension_id, proposed_action (sandbox|suspend|terminate|quarantine), confidence (fixed-point), evidence_hashes, policy_version, signature.
3. **QuorumCheckpoint**: Periodic fleet evidence state checkpoint. Fields: checkpoint_seq (monotonic), evidence_head_hashes per node, aggregated posterior snapshot, quorum_signatures (sorted by key for determinism), epoch.
4. **ReconciliationRequest**: Anti-entropy request for evidence gaps. Fields: node_id, known_evidence_frontier, requested_range, signature.

### Convergence SLO
- 90% of containment decisions converge fleet-wide within 10s under normal operation
- 99% convergence within 30s including degraded-mode recovery
- Per-decision convergence timestamp tracked via observability surface

title: Unify duplicate JSON builtin capability names and ABI
description: Review of 8431216e found it added batch-36 mappings 365-366 to builtin:JSONStringify and builtin:JSONParse at crates/franken-engine/src/baseline_interpreter.rs:19492-19493, while the existing JSON mappings at lines 19216-19217 still use builtin:JsonParse and builtin:JsonStringify. Current dispatch has separate implementations for both naming schemes: JsonStringify/JsonParse at lines 8353-8425 and JSONStringify/JSONParse at lines 18391-18444. The two paths use different argument conventions (older reads args.start, batch-36 reads args.start + 1) and different semantics (for example JsonStringify escapes quotes and backslashes and handles NaN/Infinity as null, while JSONStringify only escapes quotes and falls through many Value variants to null). This makes JSON behavior depend on which function index produced the capability rather than the JS API. Keep one canonical JSON capability naming scheme and implementation, normalize mappings 70/71 and 365/366, and add regression tests that both map paths exercise identical JSON parse/stringify behavior.

title: [10.9] Release gate: deterministic IFC protections block unauthorized sensitive-source exfiltration across the published exfil corpus, with receipt-backed declassification audit for approved exceptions (implementation ownership: `10.15` + `10.5` + `10.7`).
description:
## Plan Reference
Section 10.9, item 8 -- Moonshot Disruption Track (release gates for frontier programs).

## What
This is a **release gate**, not an implementation task. It verifies that deterministic Information Flow Control (IFC) protections -- built by the Delta Moonshots track (10.15), the Security track (10.5), and the Conformance track (10.7) -- successfully block all unauthorized sensitive-source exfiltration attempts across the published exfiltration corpus. The gate also confirms that approved exceptions (legitimate data flows that cross security boundaries) are covered by receipt-backed declassification audit trails.

The gate owner does not build the IFC system; the gate owner runs the exfiltration corpus against the deployed IFC protections and certifies the pass/fail evidence bundle.

## Gate Criteria
1. The published exfiltration corpus (a curated set of exfil vectors: direct channel, covert timing channel, storage channel, network side-channel, prototype chain leak, etc.) is executed against FrankenEngine with IFC enabled.
2. Every unauthorized exfiltration attempt in the corpus is blocked (0% success rate for unauthorized flows).
3. For each blocked attempt, a structured blocking receipt is produced containing: flow source label, flow destination label, blocking policy rule, timestamp, and receipt signature.
4. Approved exceptions (declassified flows) are explicitly listed in a declassification policy, and each approved flow produces a signed declassification receipt containing: declassification justification, approver identity, policy version, and receipt signature.
5. The IFC enforcement is deterministic: replaying the same exfil corpus against the same engine configuration and policy version produces bit-identical blocking/declassification decisions.
6. No IFC bypass exists through reflection, dynamic code generation (eval/Function), or native addon escape hatches -- the corpus includes vectors targeting these paths.

## Implementation Ownership
- **10.15 (Delta Moonshots):** Builds the IFC enforcement runtime and declassification receipt infrastructure. Encompasses 9I moonshots: IFC, Security-Proof-Guided Specialization, TEE-Bound Receipts.
- **10.5 (Security):** Defines the exfiltration corpus, security label taxonomy, and declassification policy framework.
- **10.7 (Conformance + Verification):** Provides the receipt verification infrastructure and conformance test harness for IFC properties.
- **10.9 (this gate):** Executes the exfiltration corpus, evaluates results against the 0% unauthorized success criterion, validates declassification receipts, and certifies the evidence bundle.

## Rationale
Deterministic IFC is one of FrankenEngine's most ambitious security claims -- no mainstream JS/TS runtime enforces information flow control at the runtime level. The claim is only credible if it holds against a comprehensive, curated exfiltration corpus that includes both obvious and subtle leak vectors. A single missed exfiltration path invalidates the guarantee. The receipt-backed declassification audit ensures that approved exceptions are explicit and accountable, not silent holes. This gate provides the primary evidence for the `security_delta` dimension of the disruption scorecard (bd-6pk).

Related 9I moonshots: IFC, Security-Proof-Guided Specialization, TEE-Bound Receipts.
Related 9F moonshots: Cryptographic Receipts, Capability-Typed TS.

## Verification Requirements
- **Full corpus execution:** Run the entire published exfiltration corpus; confirm 0% unauthorized success rate with no exceptions.
- **Blocking receipt validation:** For a representative sample of blocked flows, verify receipt signatures independently using the published trust anchor.
- **Declassification audit:** For every approved exception, confirm a signed declassification receipt exists with a justification traceable to the declassification policy.
- **Determinism test:** Run the corpus twice with identical configuration; confirm bit-identical blocking/declassification decisions.
- **Bypass vector coverage:** Confirm the corpus includes vectors targeting: eval/Function, Proxy/Reflect, native addons, SharedArrayBuffer, structured clone, and any FrankenEngine-specific escape surfaces.
- **Scorecard integration:** Results feed `security_delta` in the disruption scorecard (bd-6pk).
- **Structured logging:** IFC validation runs emit structured logs with fields: `trace_id`, `exfil_vector_id`, `source_label`, `dest_label`, `action` (block/declassify), `policy_rule`, `receipt_hash`, `receipt_signature_valid`.

## Dependencies
- bd-6pk (disruption scorecard) -- gate results feed `security_delta` dimension.
- bd-3rd (adversarial campaign runner gate) -- adversarial campaigns may include IFC bypass attempts; results should be consistent.
- bd-uwc (quarantine mesh gate) -- quarantine mesh may trigger IFC-related isolation.
- 10.15 Delta Moonshots track -- delivers IFC enforcement runtime.
- 10.5 Security track -- delivers exfiltration corpus and declassification policy.
- 10.7 Conformance + Verification track -- delivers receipt verification infrastructure.
- bd-1xm (parent epic) -- this bead is a child of the Moonshot Disruption Track epic.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Implement the full objective with explicit deterministic behavior, failure semantics, and rollback constraints where applicable.
2. Add focused unit tests covering normal paths, boundary conditions, invalid or adversarial inputs, and invariant enforcement.
3. Add end-to-end or integration test scripts that exercise lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths using deterministic seeds or fixtures and CI-ready command lines.
4. Emit structured logs with stable fields (trace_id, decision_id, policy_id, component, event, outcome, error_code) and add assertions for critical log events in tests.
5. Produce reproducibility artifacts (run manifest, replay/evidence pointers, benchmark/check outputs) and document operator verification steps.
6. For Rust build or test workflows introduced by this bead, document or execute via rch-wrapped commands for heavy compilation or test workloads.

## Detailed Requirements (Plan-Space Refinement)
- This bead is a release gate and may only close when every declared dependency gate/input is closed with signed and reproducible artifacts.
- Produce a deterministic gate-check runbook (CLI commands, expected outputs, failure codes) that can be executed by an independent operator.
- Attach threshold tables for pass/fail metrics (security, performance, determinism, replay, operational safety) and document rationale for each threshold.
- Include explicit rollback/fallback activation criteria and validated recovery commands for gate failure scenarios.
- Require gate-specific end-to-end validation scripts and structured log assertions proving the gate result is reproducible and auditable.

title: [IDEA-WIZARD] Live swarm snapshot bridge and proof recovery plan
description:
## Background
Current SWARM control surfaces are intentionally fixture-fed and advisory-only. That is correct for safety, but it leaves operators and agents doing manual glue work: copy br status, Agent Mail reservations, git dirty state, rch worker state, and failed proof transcripts into separate gates. In a massive swarm on 64+ cores and 256GB+ RAM, that manual glue becomes the bottleneck and causes duplicate work, local cargo fallback, stale ownership, and unclear proof recovery.

## Idea-wizard phase 2: 30 ideas considered, top 5 selected
Generated candidates included live read-only snapshot capture, rch failure capsules, cargo error clustering, claim freshness decay alarms, cross-SWARM artifact doctor, target heat maps, proof cache reuse, high-core chaos replay, Agent Mail SLA panels, no-local-cargo preflight, worker toolchain truth ledgers, dependency-aware proof portfolios, stalled bead rescue, frankentui cockpit handoff, evidence redaction, runbook truth gates, remote artifact mirroring, compile blocker auto-filing, queue fairness simulations, and claim-to-proof auto-linking.

Top 5 selected because they are useful, pragmatic, and non-duplicative with existing fixture-only planners:
1. Live read-only swarm snapshot bridge: captures real br/git/rch/mail/system evidence into deterministic JSON inputs for existing gates without mutating anything.
2. RCH proof failure capsules: preserve failed remote proof context and recommend the next narrow command instead of forcing agents to rediscover failures.
3. Current-head compile error clustering: turns broad cargo failure noise into blocker proposals with exact file/error clusters.
4. Claim freshness decay alarms: warns when README/operator claims are drifting away from fresh evidence.
5. Cross-SWARM artifact doctor: checks bundles for missing files, local fallback markers, stale hashes, incomplete manifests, and broken replay pointers.

## Idea-wizard phase 3: next best 10 kept as explicit follow-ons
6. Worker target-dir heat map.
7. Proof-cache reuse ROI feedback loop.
8. Agent Mail response-SLA panel.
9. Stalled ownership reopen recommender with receipt evidence.
10. Dependency-aware proof portfolio optimizer.
11. RCH worker toolchain drift detector.
12. Operator SLO what-changed-since-green diff.
13. Claim-to-proof auto-linker for README sections.
14. High-core chaos replay expansion.
15. Bead graph quality gate for idea-wizard output.

## Non-goals
- Do not turn fixture-fed gates into mutating live schedulers.
- Do not run Cargo locally.
- Do not replace /dp/frankentui, /dp/frankensqlite, or /dp/sqlmodel_rust.
- Do not query or mutate Agent Mail from a production gate unless the command is explicitly read-only and optional; file snapshots are acceptable.

## Acceptance
The child beads define contracts, scripts, tests, and operator docs that preserve advisory-only behavior while making live evidence capture and proof recovery repeatable.
notes: Phase 4/6 refinement: overlap check found closed bd-eozx0 already owns the canonical live swarm operations state contract and bd-x82vp already owns the resource lease planner. This epic is therefore scoped as a bridge/extension and proof-recovery package: reuse bd-eozx0 for canonical state fields, reuse bd-x82vp for lease/admission semantics, and add missing read-only capture profiles, provenance/redaction hardening, downstream dashboard/operator-status composition, failed-proof capsules, compile-error clustering, claim freshness alarms, and artifact-doctor coverage. Do not duplicate the existing live state contract or lease planner.

Implement a deterministic shell/JSON normalizer that assembles a read-only capture-profile bundle compatible with the existing bd-eozx0 live swarm state contract and downstream SWARM gates.

## Why
Operators need one reproducible input bundle for existing resource lease, admission, operator status, and dashboard gates. This lowers coordination friction without giving the engine repo a live scheduler or duplicating bd-eozx0/bd-x82vp.

## How

If a source is missing, emit degraded evidence instead of silently omitting it. Write snapshot.json, events.jsonl, commands.txt, redaction_report.json, and report.md.

## Risks
Do not run Cargo. Do not mutate br, git, Agent Mail, rch workers, target dirs, or artifacts. Reject transcripts showing mutating commands unless explicitly marked as external evidence. Do not replace the existing resource lease planner.

## Acceptance
- bash -n passes for the script.
- check/selftest fixture runs produce stable JSON and markdown reports.
- Missing/stale/malformed sources fail closed or degrade with explicit reasons.
- Local rch fallback markers are preserved as risk evidence, not hidden.

## What
Add an optional capture adapter/runbook that shows agents how to collect read-only br, git, rch, and Agent Mail snapshots for the snapshot bundle.

## Why
The normalizer should be fixture-friendly, but users need an ergonomic path from live state to fixture files. A read-only adapter makes the bridge repeatable while preserving safety boundaries.

## How

Every command must be listed in commands.txt with mutation_class=read_only.

## Risks
Agent Mail may not have a stable shell CLI. Treat its input as optional file data, not a hard dependency. Never claim beads, release reservations, restart rch, run cargo, or clean target dirs.

## Acceptance
- Adapter refuses mutating command patterns such as br update, br close, git add/commit/reset, rch workers disable, cargo, rm, or cleanup commands.
- Captured snapshots can round-trip through the bundle writer.
- Operator docs include exact examples and degraded-mode behavior.

title: [RCH-PROOF-CAPSULE] Capture failed remote proof capsules and next-command advice
description:
## What
Create a proof-failure capsule lane that preserves failed rch proof context and emits a deterministic next-command recommendation.

## Why
Agents currently lose time rediscovering broad compile failures, local fallback markers, stale target dirs, and worker/toolchain issues. A capsule turns failed proof output into reusable evidence and avoids repeating unsafe or unproductive commands.

## How
Design a shell/JSON gate that consumes rch transcript snippets, command metadata, worker id, exit code, timing, first relevant compiler errors, target dir, and local fallback markers. Emit proof_failure_capsule.json, next_command_advice.json, commands.txt, events.jsonl, and report.md.

## Risks
The advice must be conservative. It should recommend narrower proof, blocker filing, or waiting for toolchain repair; it must not run cargo itself or claim success from failed output.

## Acceptance
- Handles remote success, remote compile failure, local fallback, queue timeout, worker toolchain missing, and interrupted build cases.
- Emits exact blocker text suitable for a bead note.
- Refuses to classify a local cargo fallback as valid proof.
- Includes shell smoke coverage and fixture transcripts.
close_reason: Added shell/JQ rch proof failure capsule with six fixture transcript scenarios, conservative next-command advice, and smoke coverage.

title: [COMPILE-BLOCKER] Cluster current-head cargo errors into blocker proposals
description:
## What
Add a deterministic analyzer that clusters failed cargo/rch compiler output into file/module/error-family groups and drafts blocker bead proposals without creating them automatically.

## Why
Current-head compile drift often blocks unrelated beads. Agents need a fast way to separate target-relevant errors from unrelated workspace drift and produce exact blocker notes.

## How
Consume saved stderr/stdout transcripts from rch-backed cargo commands. Extract rustc error codes, file paths, first diagnostics, package/target, command, worker id, and whether tests reached the intended target. Emit compile_blocker_clusters.json, proposed_beads.md, events.jsonl, and report.md.

## Risks
The tool must not invent bugs from truncated output or create beads automatically. It should mark confidence and require human/agent review before br create.

## Acceptance
- Fixtures cover target-relevant first error, unrelated sibling errors, stale test APIs, local fallback contamination, and truncated output.
- Proposed bead text includes exact command, first error lines, and validation scope.
- Output differentiates block-current-bead versus file-follow-up versus infra/toolchain blocker.
close_reason: Added read-only rch compile blocker clusterer with proposal markdown and fixture smoke coverage for target, unrelated, stale API, local fallback, and truncated output cases.

title: [CLAIM-FRESHNESS] Add evidence age decay alarms for README and operator claims
description:
## What
Add an advisory claim freshness gate that flags README/operator/runbook claims whose backing artifact bundles are missing, stale, degraded, or from a different code revision.

## Why
The runtime charter requires claim language to match evidence. As SWARM gates multiply, users need a single decay alarm that says when observed wording is no longer backed by fresh proof.

## How
Consume claim_to_proof_matrix_v1.json, README claim-sensitive sections, selected SWARM contract metadata, and artifact manifest timestamps/hashes. Emit claim_freshness_report.json, downgrade_suggestions.md, events.jsonl, commands.txt, and report.md.

## Risks
The gate should not rewrite docs automatically. It should produce precise suggested downgrade text and source locations for review.

## Acceptance
- Fixtures cover fresh observed claim, stale observed claim, missing artifact, degraded artifact, and target/hypothesis wording that remains allowed.
- Report includes claim id, file/section, artifact path, artifact age, code revision, decision, and suggested wording.
- README and runtime charter wording remain aligned.

title: [ARTIFACT-DOCTOR] Add cross-SWARM bundle doctor for evidence integrity

## Why
Operators rely on many SWARM bundles. A single missing step log or stale manifest can make a replay look trustworthy when it is not. A doctor gives fast, uniform diagnostics before claims or dashboards consume the bundle.

## How

## Acceptance
